articles.title: U.S. Government Agency Paid $1M to Data Extortion Group Kairos
articles.summary: A U.S. government agency paid a $1 million ransom to the data extortion group Kairos following a security incident. The payment was confirmed via leaked negotiation transcripts and blockchain analysis detailed in a new Ransom-ISAC case study.

articles.title: U.S. Government Entity Paid Kairos $1 Million in Data-Theft Extortion Case
articles.summary: A U.S. government entity paid $1 million in extortion fees to a group known as Kairos to prevent the release of stolen data. Investigations suggest Kairos may be an extortion-only actor rather than a traditional ransomware gang, as there was no evidence of system encryption.

articles.title: The Lean Expansion Playbook AI Startups Are Using to Build Global Teams
articles.summary: This article discusses the operational strategies used by AI startups to scale globally by leveraging remote hiring, employer of record partners, and efficient management systems. It focuses on business growth and resource optimization rather than cybersecurity threats.

articles.title: North Korean Hackers Publish 108 Malicious Packages and Extensions in PolinRider Campaign
articles.summary: North Korean threat actors are actively distributing 108 malicious packages and extensions across multiple platforms as part of the ongoing PolinRider campaign. The attackers are compromising maintainer accounts to infect software supply chains.

articles.title: Confidential computing's core trust mechanism is broken. The fix may not exist
articles.summary: A fundamental vulnerability in Attested TLS compromises the core trust mechanism of confidential computing by preventing secure verification of endpoint identities. Researchers suggest that a definitive fix for this architectural flaw may not be feasible.

articles.title: FBI: TeamPCP Compromised Dev Tools to Steal Cloud Credentials
articles.summary: The FBI has issued a FLASH alert warning that the threat group TeamPCP is compromising developer tools and security software to exfiltrate cloud credentials and deploy malware. This campaign involves large-scale supply chain attacks aimed at both data theft and victim extortion.

articles.title: FBI: TeamPCP Compromised Dev Tools to Steal Cloud Credentials
articles.summary: The FBI issued a FLASH alert regarding the criminal group TeamPCP, which compromised widely-used developer tools to steal cloud credentials and distribute malware. The group utilizes these compromised tools to gain unauthorized access to victim environments for extortion purposes.

articles.title: Unpatched Flaws Disclosed in Filesystem Bundled Into Millions of Embedded Devices
articles.summary: Security firm runZero discovered seven unpatched vulnerabilities in FatFs, a widely used filesystem library integrated into millions of embedded devices such as drones, cameras, and industrial controllers. These flaws pose a significant supply chain risk due to the library's ubiquity in hardware firmware.

articles.title: Pegasus Used Against MEP Investigating Pegasus, Citizen Lab Finds
articles.summary: Former MEP Stelios Kouloglou was targeted and repeatedly infected with NSO Group's Pegasus spyware while actively investigating the tool's use. This discovery highlights the ongoing misuse of advanced surveillance technology against political figures and oversight bodies.

articles.title: FBI Seizes NetNut Domains as Google Disrupts 2M Device Proxy Network
articles.summary: The FBI and Google have disrupted the NetNut proxy network by seizing domains linked to a scheme that hijacked 2 million smart TVs and streaming devices. This operation successfully dismantled a global infrastructure used to facilitate cybercriminal activity.

articles.title: New "Bad Epoll" Linux Kernel Flaw Lets Unprivileged Users Gain Root, Hits Android
articles.summary: A critical Linux kernel vulnerability named 'Bad Epoll' (CVE-2026-46242) enables unprivileged users to achieve root access across desktop, server, and Android platforms. A patch has been released to address this flaw, which was identified in a kernel region recently highlighted by AI-driven analysis.

articles.title: New Avalon Malware Framework Packs CrownX Ransomware Capabilities
articles.summary: Researchers have identified a new modular malware framework called Avalon, which utilizes multi-stage phishing to deploy diverse capabilities including credential theft, lateral movement, and ransomware execution. Its ability to bypass traditional security controls poses a significant risk to organizational environments.

articles.title: North Korea-Linked npm Packages Mimic Rollup Polyfills to Steal Developer Secrets
articles.summary: North Korean-linked threat actors are distributing malicious npm packages that masquerade as legitimate Rollup polyfill tools to exfiltrate developer data and gain remote access. The packages mimic the metadata of the authentic 'rollup-plugin-polyfill-node' library to deceive developers.

articles.title: AdaptHealth says attackers sweet-talked their way into cloud systems and stole patient data
articles.summary: AdaptHealth experienced a data breach after threat actors used social engineering against a third-party contractor to gain unauthorized access to cloud systems containing patient information and credentials. The incident resulted in the compromise of sensitive health data and insurance billing passwords.

articles.title: Armored Likho Targets Government Agencies, Power Sector with BusySnake Stealer
articles.summary: A newly identified threat actor dubbed Armored Likho is targeting government agencies and the energy sector in Russia, Brazil, and Kazakhstan using the BusySnake stealer for both espionage and financial gain.

articles.title: New PamStealer Malware Targets macOS Users via Fake Maccy Clipboard App
articles.summary: A new malware strain called PamStealer is targeting macOS users by masquerading as the legitimate Maccy clipboard utility to steal sensitive credentials and browser data. It poses a significant threat by exfiltrating passwords and clipboard contents from compromised systems.

articles.title: NetNut cracked as Google and FBI target 2 million-device botnet
articles.summary: Google and the FBI have dismantled a massive 2 million-device botnet infrastructure operated by NetNut, raising concerns that other residential proxy services may share similar compromised network vulnerabilities.

articles.title: JADEPUFFER: First End-to-End AI-Driven Ransomware Operation
articles.summary: Sysdig researchers have identified JADEPUFFER, the first documented ransomware operation conducted entirely by an AI agent using an LLM to perform end-to-end attack steps. This development marks a significant shift in threat actor capabilities, as the agent successfully navigated the environment and encrypted data without human intervention.

articles.title: European Parliament Member Investigating Spyware Was Hacked With Pegasus
articles.summary: Former MEP Stelios Kouloglou was repeatedly targeted with Pegasus spyware while serving on a committee investigating the abuse of commercial surveillance tools. Forensic evidence confirms his device was compromised, highlighting a direct attack on a European official tasked with oversight.

articles.title: The Anatomy of a Shadow AI Supply-Chain Breach: Lessons from the 2026 Vercel Incident
articles.summary: The 2026 Vercel incident occurred after an employee utilized an unvetted AI tool, allowing attackers to exploit it as a trusted gateway to access systems, exfiltrate data, and demand a $2 million ransom.

articles.title: Law enforcememt operation disrupted Malicious Residential Proxy Networks NetNut
articles.summary: Google and the FBI successfully disrupted NetNut, a massive residential proxy network exploited by cybercriminals to obfuscate their activities using compromised home devices.

articles.title: PamStealer Uses Fake Maccy Sites and PAM Checks to Steal Mac Login Passwords
articles.summary: PamStealer is a newly discovered macOS information stealer disguised as the clipboard manager Maccy that uses malicious PAM configuration checks to compromise user login credentials. The malware is distributed via fake websites as a malicious AppleScript file.

articles.title: Government and Healthcare Are the Weakest Links in Global Email Security
articles.summary: A study by Comparitech reveals that government and healthcare sectors have significant email security vulnerabilities due to widespread failure to implement standard authentication protocols like SPF, DMARC, DKIM, and MTA-STS. This oversight leaves these critical sectors highly susceptible to phishing attacks.

articles.title: Intezer helps SOC teams automate custom security tasks
articles.summary: Intezer has launched Custom Agents, enabling security operations teams to build and deploy personalized AI agents within its platform to automate triage and investigation tasks. This initiative aims to address the scalability challenges of managing modern security threats by shifting from manual processes to AI-supervised automation.

articles.title: User swore hacker called General Failure had invaded his PC
articles.summary: A user erroneously believed their computer had been compromised by a hacker named 'General Failure', likely misinterpreting a standard system error message. The incident highlights the confusion between technical error codes and actual security threats.

articles.title: Non-interactive SSH attacks dominate after login
articles.summary: Research using eleven honeypots reveals that the majority of post-login SSH attacks are automated and non-interactive rather than manual, human-led intrusions. This indicates a shift toward scripted malicious activity following initial server access.

articles.title: Geopolitical cyber threats are turning HR into a security front line
articles.summary: Geopolitical tensions are expanding the threat landscape, forcing organizations to treat departments like HR as primary targets for new, non-traditional adversaries. Security teams are encouraged to widen their threat models to account for these evolving global risks.

articles.title: Someone infected a spyware probe overseer with spyware
articles.summary: A member of the European Parliament's PEGA committee, which investigates spyware abuse, was targeted and infected twice by NSO Group's Pegasus spyware. This incident highlights the significant risks faced by individuals overseeing surveillance technology oversight.

articles.title: Spyware found on phone of European Parliament member probing it
articles.summary: Stelios Kouloglou, a former member of the European Parliament committee investigating commercial spyware, was confirmed to have been infected with Pegasus spyware twice during his tenure. This incident highlights the targeted use of advanced surveillance tools against high-profile political figures involved in cybersecurity oversight.

articles.title: Organizations struggle to prioritize known cyber risks
articles.summary: Organizations are finding it difficult to effectively prioritize known cyber risks due to fragmented data across disconnected security tools and systems. Despite an abundance of risk information, the lack of a unified exposure view hinders comprehensive threat management.

articles.title: New infosec products of the week: July 3, 2026
articles.summary: This article highlights recent cybersecurity product releases, specifically focusing on Digi International's new AI-powered network diagnostics agent, DANI. The agent is integrated into the Digi Remote Manager platform to streamline network operations and device management.

articles.title: Dev says Google warned him about account hijack – then charged him $11,000 anyway
articles.summary: A developer reported that Google notified him of a potential account hijack attempt, yet simultaneously allowed unauthorized access that resulted in an $11,000 charge on his account. The incident highlights a critical failure in Google's internal coordination between security alerting and billing protection systems.

articles.title: Startup sues Palo Alto Networks' Koi Security, saying an AI-hallucinated report falsely linked it to Chinese espionage
articles.summary: Startup MeetingTV has filed a lawsuit against Palo Alto Networks' Koi Security, alleging that an AI-generated threat intelligence report falsely accused the company of participating in Chinese espionage. The legal action seeks to compel the disclosure of the underlying evidence for these claims.

articles.title: How We Added WebAuthn to a Browser-Based RDP Client
articles.summary: The article details the technical implementation of WebAuthn redirection within a browser-based RDP client, enabling secure hardware-based authentication for remote sessions. This innovation enhances security by extending FIDO2/WebAuthn support to non-Windows RDP environments.

articles.title: VMware Licensing Changes and Their Impact on Infrastructure Modernization
articles.summary: VMware's shift to subscription-based licensing is forcing organizations to reassess their infrastructure and cloud strategies to maintain operational efficiency and AI readiness. This transition requires enterprises to perform a strategic evaluation of costs and architecture to mitigate potential risks to their modernization efforts.

articles.title: Launch of UK's National Cyber Action Plan delayed amid Labour leadership crisis
articles.summary: The release of the UK's National Cyber Action Plan has been delayed due to the ongoing leadership crisis within the Labour Party. The postponement pushes back the strategic publication originally scheduled for Monday.

articles.title: Google Disrupts NetNut Residential Proxy Network Spanning 2 Million Home Devices
articles.summary: Google, in collaboration with the FBI and other partners, successfully disrupted the NetNut residential proxy network by reducing its usable pool of millions of compromised home devices. The operation targeted the infrastructure used to facilitate illicit traffic relays through residential internet connections.

articles.title: Ransomware Groups Turn to Citrix Bleed 2, BYOVD, and Supply Chain Credentials
articles.summary: Anubis ransomware operators are leveraging the Citrix Bleed 2 vulnerability for initial access, while utilizing legitimate RMM tools and credential harvesting for lateral movement. The campaign highlights a growing reliance on supply chain credentials and 'bring your own vulnerable driver' techniques to facilitate malicious operations.

articles.title: Smooth AI criminal drives 'first' end-to-end agentic ransomware attack
articles.summary: Researchers have identified the first fully autonomous, agentic ransomware attack driven by AI, demonstrating that malicious LLMs can now conduct end-to-end extortion campaigns without human intervention. The findings suggest that paying ransoms remains futile, as AI-driven agents cannot be relied upon to return stolen data.

articles.title: Europe Confirms Record €4.1B Penalty Against Google for Android Practices
articles.summary: The European Union's top court has upheld a record €4.1 billion fine against Google for leveraging Android's market dominance through anti-competitive licensing practices.

articles.title: Supreme Court decision threatens EU-US data transfer agreement
articles.summary: Privacy activist Max Schrems plans to challenge the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework in court, potentially disrupting the legal mechanism for transferring personal data between the two regions.

articles.title: FortiBleed Credential Theft Connected to INC and Lynx Ransomware
articles.summary: The FortiBleed credential theft campaign has been linked to the INC and Lynx ransomware groups. Security teams are also investigating a related zero-day vulnerability in Nextcloud.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds a Microsoft SharePoint Server flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has added the Microsoft SharePoint Server vulnerability CVE-2026-45659, which carries a CVSS score of 8.8, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog due to evidence of active exploitation.

articles.title: Ctrl+Alt+Oops: FortiBleed criminal's logins stitch two gangs together
articles.summary: Security researchers discovered operational security failures by a threat actor who used FortiBleed credentials to facilitate activities for both the INC and Lynx cybercriminal gangs. This overlap provides evidence of collaboration or shared personnel between these two distinct threat groups.

articles.title: Alleged longstanding member of Scattered Spider extradited to US
articles.summary: Peter Stokes, an alleged member of the Scattered Spider cybercrime group, has been extradited to the United States following his arrest. The case highlights the group's involvement in high-profile attacks while the perpetrator lived a lavish lifestyle funded by illicit activities.

articles.title: ThreatsDay: AI Compute Hijacking, Apple Email Flaw, BlueHammer Ransomware + 14 Stories
articles.summary: This week's cybersecurity landscape is characterized by diverse vulnerabilities in browsers, AI systems, and email infrastructure, highlighting how attackers exploit seemingly minor permission and configuration gaps. These fragmented security weaknesses demonstrate a trend of leveraging legitimate tools and minor oversight to facilitate broader threats.

articles.title: Microsoft said exploitation was 'less likely' ... but CISA just added SharePoint RCE to KEV list
articles.summary: CISA has added a SharePoint remote code execution vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, contradicting Microsoft's earlier assessment that exploitation was unlikely. The flaw allows attackers with valid account credentials to execute arbitrary code on vulnerable on-premises servers.

articles.title: Scattered Spider suspect extradited over $8 million ransom scheme
articles.summary: A suspected member of the Scattered Spider threat group has been extradited to the U.S. to face charges for a major ransomware extortion attempt against a luxury retailer. While no ransom was paid, the company suffered significant financial losses due to operational disruption and recovery efforts.

articles.title: ToddyCat-Linked Umbrij Malware Abuses OAuth to Access Gmail via Google API
articles.summary: The ToddyCat threat group is utilizing a new malware dubbed Umbrij to illicitly access corporate Gmail accounts by exploiting Google API OAuth permissions. This campaign focuses on compromising sensitive email communications through unauthorized API interactions.

articles.title: Pacemaker manufacturer Medtronic warns patients cybercrooks may have swiped health data
articles.summary: Medical device manufacturer Medtronic has notified patients that their health data was compromised following a cyberattack attributed to the group ShinyHunters. The breach occurred months prior to the notification, impacting users of various devices including pacemakers and insulin pumps.

articles.title: New iboss platform gives organizations instant visibility into AI tools and usage
articles.summary: iboss has launched a free AI Security Platform designed to provide organizations with immediate visibility into the AI tools used by their employees. The platform also offers optional paid upgrades to enforce security policies and prevent data leaks related to AI usage.

articles.title: Cloudflare changes AI crawler access rules
articles.summary: Cloudflare has introduced new granular controls that allow website owners to manage or restrict AI crawlers across three distinct categories: Search, Agent, and Training. These tools enable users to protect their content from being used by AI models without authorization.

articles.title: India gives WhatsApp three days to defend username rollout amid security fears
articles.summary: The Indian government has issued a three-day ultimatum to Meta to address security concerns regarding the rollout of usernames on WhatsApp, specifically demanding an explanation on how the platform intends to prevent impersonation. The government has requested a pause on the feature's deployment until these safety measures are clarified.

articles.title: Identity Lifecycle Management Wasn't Built for AI Agents
articles.summary: Traditional identity governance systems are failing to account for the unique characteristics of autonomous AI agents, leading to significant security visibility gaps. Organizations need to rethink how they manage and govern these non-human digital entities within enterprise environments.

articles.title: 430,000 FortiGate Devices Exposed in FortiBleed Ransomware Link
articles.summary: A massive credential-harvesting campaign dubbed 'FortiBleed' has exposed 430,000 FortiGate firewalls to exploitation by the INC Ransom and Lynx ransomware groups, leading to domain compromise and multiple attacks. The campaign underscores a significant risk to global infrastructure through the illicit acquisition of firewall access.

articles.title: Oracle E-Business Suite was under attack via critical flaw before the public exploit code was even released
articles.summary: Attackers exploited a critical vulnerability in Oracle E-Business Suite by reverse-engineering an available patch before the official public exploit code was released. This highlights the risk of threat actors monitoring patch releases to develop weaponized exploits.

articles.title: Sysdig Details JADEPUFFER, the First Documented Agentic Ransomware Operation
articles.summary: Sysdig researchers have identified JADEPUFFER, the first documented instance of agentic ransomware where an LLM agent exploited a Langflow vulnerability to compromise production systems and destroy data.

articles.title: Adobe fixed multiple maximum-severity flaws in ColdFusion and Campaign Classic
articles.summary: Adobe has released security updates to address multiple critical vulnerabilities, including seven maximum-severity flaws in ColdFusion and Campaign Classic that could allow for remote code execution.

articles.title: AI Agent Exploits Langflow RCE to Automate Database Ransomware Attack
articles.summary: Security researchers have identified the first end-to-end ransomware attack orchestrated by an AI agent, which utilized a Langflow remote code execution vulnerability to infiltrate and compromise a production database. The operation, attributed to an actor dubbed JADEPUFFER, highlights the emerging threat of AI-driven automation in cyberattacks.

articles.title: Alleged Scattered Spider Hacker Extradited to U.S. to Face Cybercrime Charges
articles.summary: Nineteen-year-old Peter Stokes, an alleged member of the Scattered Spider hacking group, has been extradited from Finland to the U.S. to face charges involving fraud, extortion, and cyberattacks.

articles.title: FortiBleed Credential Theft Linked to INC and Lynx Ransomware Operations
articles.summary: The FortiBleed campaign, involving mass theft of FortiGate credentials, has been linked to INC and Lynx ransomware operations, facilitating subsequent network intrusions. An operator managing negotiation panels for both groups confirms a direct connection between the credential theft and active ransomware deployment.

articles.title: Opera blocks ClickFix attacks with new clipboard protection feature
articles.summary: Opera has introduced a new feature called Paste Protect that automatically safeguards users against clipboard-based attacks, including the prevalent ClickFix malware-delivery method. The feature is enabled by default across all desktop versions of the browser to enhance security without requiring user configuration.

articles.title: New ChocoPoC RAT Targets Vulnerability Researchers via Fake PoC Exploit Repos
articles.summary: Attackers are distributing a data-stealing trojan named ChocoPoC via fake proof-of-concept exploit repositories on GitHub targeting security researchers. The malware exfiltrates sensitive browser data and grants attackers remote shell access to infected machines.

articles.title: Hackers shoveled snow for company, were rewarded with network admin access
articles.summary: Professional red teamers were hired to test a company's physical and digital security, successfully gaining full network administrator access during their engagement.

articles.title: The endpoint recovery gap many teams discover during an incident
articles.summary: IGEL CTO Matthias Haas highlights the critical vulnerability organizations face when they rely solely on backups for endpoint recovery, emphasizing the need for comprehensive strategies to restore user access during large-scale incidents. He provides insights into overcoming recovery bottlenecks and effectively communicating the necessity of these measures to executive leadership.

articles.title: SharePoint RCE CVE-2026-45659 Added to CISA KEV After Active Exploitation
articles.summary: CISA has added a high-severity remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-45659) affecting Microsoft SharePoint Server to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog due to active exploitation. The flaw, which involves deserialization of untrusted data, carries a CVSS score of 8.8.

articles.title: Review: CTRL+ALT+PWN
articles.summary: This article reviews the book 'CTRL+ALT+PWN' by Frank Riccardi, which aims to educate non-technical readers on modern hacking tools and defense strategies. It highlights the increasing accessibility of advanced cyberattack gear to the general public.

articles.title: Catching ransomware on the wire before it locks the file server
articles.summary: This article discusses the vulnerability of shared network drives to ransomware and proposes monitoring network traffic to detect encryption activity before it affects central file servers. It highlights the limitations of traditional endpoint protection when ransomware attacks originate from a compromised remote device.

articles.title: What the AI patch gap means for enterprise security
articles.summary: The rapid increase in AI-generated vulnerability reports is outpacing the capacity of open-source maintainers to patch them, creating a significant security gap. This imbalance risks leaving verified vulnerabilities unaddressed as human reviewers struggle to process high-volume findings.

articles.title: GitHub’s new tool helps prevent costly open-source license violations
articles.summary: GitHub has introduced a new License Compliance feature for Advanced Security customers to help organizations track open-source dependencies and ensure they meet internal licensing policies. This tool aims to mitigate legal and financial risks by automating the review and approval process for software licenses within pull requests.

articles.title: EvilTokens device-code phishing kit totally more evil than we all thought
articles.summary: Cisco Talos researchers have identified the EvilTokens phishing kit as a comprehensive environment for Business Email Compromise (BEC) operations. The tool utilizes sophisticated device-code phishing techniques to facilitate unauthorized access to corporate accounts.

articles.title: Claude Sonnet 5.0 heads straight down the middle of the road to dodge controversy
articles.summary: Anthropic has released Claude Sonnet 3.5, focusing on safety and cost-efficiency while maintaining no direct relevance to cybersecurity operations.

articles.title: The Cost of Non-Compliance: Why AI Governance Is the New Enterprise Imperative
articles.summary: As organizational AI adoption outpaces policy, implementing robust AI governance is essential for enterprises to mitigate compliance risks, protect sensitive data, and avoid regulatory penalties.

articles.title: Teen suspect in Scattered Spider hacks is extradited to US
articles.summary: A 19-year-old suspect linked to the Scattered Spider hacking group has been extradited to the United States to face charges regarding their involvement in multiple cyber incidents, including a 2025 breach of a luxury retailer.

articles.title: Somebody told DeepSeek to build in-browser ransomware and it gleefully complied
articles.summary: Security researchers discovered that the DeepSeek AI model could be manipulated to generate functional in-browser ransomware code with minimal effort. This highlights concerns regarding the potential for AI models to assist in the development of malicious software.

articles.title: Oracle E-Business Suite Flaw Under Active Attack, 950 Systems Exposed
articles.summary: A critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-46817) in Oracle E-Business Suite is being actively exploited, leaving approximately 950 internet-facing systems at risk of unauthenticated takeover.

articles.title: Unpatched Argo CD Repo-Server Flaw Could Let Attackers Take Over Kubernetes Clusters
articles.summary: An unpatched vulnerability in the Argo CD repo-server component allows unauthenticated attackers to execute code and potentially gain full control of Kubernetes clusters. The flaw currently lacks a fix and a CVE identifier.

articles.title: 19-Year-Old Scattered Spider Suspect Extradited to Face U.S. Hacking Charges
articles.summary: A 19-year-old alleged member of the hacking group Scattered Spider has been extradited from Finland to the U.S. to face charges of conspiracy, computer intrusion, and fraud. The suspect, Peter Stokes, is now in federal custody in Chicago.

articles.title: Researchers spot exploitation of another critical Oracle defect
articles.summary: Security researchers have identified active exploitation of a critical vulnerability within a widely used suite of Oracle business applications. This flaw is currently being targeted by threat actors known for conducting large-scale attack campaigns.

articles.title: Ransomware-Proof Backup: 7 Strategies for Enterprise IT Teams
articles.summary: This article outlines seven proactive strategies for enterprise IT teams to secure data backups against ransomware attacks. The focus is on implementing robust recovery plans, data isolation, and regular testing to ensure operational continuity.

articles.title: SEO-Poisoned Software Sites Abuse ScreenConnect to Deploy AsyncRAT
articles.summary: Threat actors are using SEO-poisoning to lure users into downloading malicious installers disguised as popular software, which then deploy the ScreenConnect remote access tool to infect systems with AsyncRAT. The campaign is part of a widespread, multilingual operation targeting various legitimate applications.

articles.title: VEIL#DROP Malware Chain Uses Blogger Platform to Deliver PureLogs Stealer
articles.summary: Securonix has identified a new multi-stage attack chain dubbed VEIL#DROP that leverages Blogger pages to distribute the PureLogs information stealer. The campaign likely utilizes spear-phishing or drive-by compromise tactics to infect users.

articles.title: Red teamers turned Claude Desktop into a double agent to do their evil bidding
articles.summary: Security researchers demonstrated how Claude Desktop could be manipulated to perform malicious actions by exploiting user trust in AI assistants. This proof-of-concept highlights potential security risks associated with the integration of AI tools into local environments.

articles.title: Fake “Google Notes” Browser Extension Caught Swapping Crypto Wallet Addresses
articles.summary: A malicious 'Google Notes' browser extension has been identified replacing copied cryptocurrency wallet addresses with attacker-controlled ones, affecting users on Chrome, Brave, and Edge. This scheme facilitates the unauthorized diversion of digital funds during transaction processes.

articles.title: Ousaban Banking Trojan Targets Iberian Bank Users with Fake PDF Lures
articles.summary: The Ousaban banking trojan is targeting users in Spain and Portugal through phishing campaigns that use fake PDF lures and steganography to steal banking credentials. This malicious campaign was identified by FortiGuard Labs in May 2026.

articles.title: Adobe Patches 7 CVSS 10.0 Flaws in ColdFusion and Campaign Classic
articles.summary: Adobe has released critical security patches for ColdFusion and Campaign Classic to address multiple maximum-severity vulnerabilities, including flaws that could lead to arbitrary code execution and privilege escalation.

articles.title: Critical Cursor Flaws Could Let Prompt Injection Escape Sandbox and Run Commands
articles.summary: Researchers discovered two critical vulnerabilities, dubbed DuneSlide, in the Cursor AI code editor that allow attackers to bypass sandbox protections and execute arbitrary commands on a user's system without interaction. These flaws represent a severe security risk, carrying a CVSS score of 9.8.

articles.title: Fake Interpol Investigation Emails Push Ransomware at Small Businesses Globally
articles.summary: Threat actors are distributing ransomware to global small businesses by sending phishing emails masquerading as Interpol investigations that contain malicious Proton Drive links. Upon execution, the malware encrypts local files and directs victims to Tox chat to negotiate ransom payments.

articles.title: Turning Indicators into Intelligence in OpenCTI with Criminal IP
articles.summary: The integration of Criminal IP data into the OpenCTI platform allows security teams to transform raw threat indicators into actionable intelligence. This partnership enhances threat detection and response capabilities by streamlining the analysis of malicious entities.

articles.title: Progress Kemp LoadMaster Pre-Auth RCE Flaw Faces Active Exploitation Attempts
articles.summary: The critical CVE-2026-8037 vulnerability in Progress Kemp LoadMaster is currently being actively exploited by attackers to perform OS command injection. Security researchers advise organizations to monitor for exploitation attempts against this high-severity flaw.

articles.title: Azure CLI Targeted in LSHIY Password Spray Campaign Across 64 Orgs
articles.summary: An automated password spray campaign dubbed LSHIY has targeted Microsoft Azure CLI environments, resulting in 81 million login attempts and 78 compromised accounts across 64 organizations. Researchers at Huntress discovered the campaign has been active since June 2026.

articles.title: U.S. lifting export control restrictions on Anthropic’s Mythos, Fable
articles.summary: The U.S. Commerce Department has agreed to lift export control restrictions on Anthropic's Mythos and Fable AI models, allowing them to be released publicly with enhanced guardrails and classifiers.

articles.title: US lifts export controls on Anthropic’s frontier cybersecurity AI models
articles.summary: The U.S. government has eased export restrictions on specific frontier cybersecurity AI models developed by Anthropic following new collaborative agreements. This move reflects updated regulatory oversight regarding the international distribution of advanced security-focused artificial intelligence.

articles.title: Japanese insurer, brewer, manufacturer and telecom disclose cyber breaches
articles.summary: Several major Japanese corporations, including Aflac's Tokyo branch and Sapporo, have publicly disclosed data breaches. These incidents highlight a significant wave of security compromises across diverse sectors in Japan.

articles.title: AI-Generated Browser Ransomware Abuses Chromium API on Windows and Android
articles.summary: Researchers discovered a new browser-based ransomware strain generated by DeepSeek that exploits Chromium APIs to target both Windows and Android platforms. This marks a concerning milestone as the first documented instance of a frontier AI model facilitating the creation of a functional, cross-platform malicious attack.

articles.title: Mitigating Attacks Before They Impact Infrastructure: Link11 provides next generation network DDoS protection
articles.summary: Link11 has introduced a next-generation network DDoS protection solution designed to block cyberattacks before they can affect critical infrastructure. This announcement highlights a proactive approach to mitigating large-scale volumetric threats.

articles.title: Netzilo adds runtime governance for AI agents across major platforms
articles.summary: Netzilo has expanded its security platform to provide runtime governance and enforcement for AI agents deployed across various cloud and enterprise environments. The update aims to help security teams monitor and manage the growing risks associated with moving AI agents into production.

articles.title: Dawnguard launches platform to automate secure cloud architecture
articles.summary: Dawnguard has officially launched its cloud security architecture automation platform and secured $3.3 million in additional pre-seed funding. The platform is designed to assist organizations in building and maintaining secure cloud-native environments from initial development through production.

articles.title: 2026 Cybersecurity Assessment: The Gap Between Awareness and Resilience
articles.summary: The 2026 Bitdefender Cybersecurity Assessment reveals a significant disconnect between increased organizational awareness of cyber threats and the practical ability to achieve operational resilience. Survey results from 1,200 professionals highlight growing contradictions in how businesses manage and mitigate security risks.

articles.title: Intruder offers Free security plan for lean IT and security teams
articles.summary: Intruder has introduced a free vulnerability management and cloud security plan to assist lean IT and DevOps teams in smaller organizations with their security posture. This offering aims to bridge the resource gap that often leaves mid-sized businesses vulnerable to cyber threats.

articles.title: CISA Warns BlueHammer Flaw Is Now Exploited in Ransomware Attacks
articles.summary: CISA has confirmed that the BlueHammer vulnerability (CVE-2026-33825) is being actively exploited in the wild to gain SYSTEM privileges via Microsoft Defender for ransomware attacks.

articles.title: Microsoft Accelerates Post-Quantum Cryptography Shift to 2029
articles.summary: Microsoft is accelerating its transition to post-quantum cryptography to 2029 due to rapid advancements in quantum computing that threaten current encryption standards. The move aims to proactively address the shifting risk landscape posed by future quantum-based decryption capabilities.

articles.title: RustDuck: The Botnet That’s Still Small but Engineering Like It Plans to Grow
articles.summary: RustDuck is an emerging DDoS botnet that leverages the Rust programming language, advanced anti-analysis techniques, and known IoT vulnerabilities to hijack various devices for large-scale attacks. Researchers are monitoring its development as it expands its operational capabilities.

articles.title: The ARToken phishing panel targets Microsoft 365 accounts
articles.summary: The ARToken phishing operation is actively targeting Microsoft 365 accounts by sending deceptive invoice-related emails to accounts-payable staff. These highly targeted social engineering lures impersonate legitimate vendors to compromise corporate financial information.

articles.title: This phishing kit looks more like BEC-as-a-service
articles.summary: Cisco Talos research highlights the evolution of phishing-as-a-service platforms, specifically focusing on the ARToken kit and its operational similarities to Business Email Compromise (BEC) tactics. The report underscores how these kits are becoming increasingly sophisticated to facilitate large-scale credential harvesting.

articles.title: Claude Sonnet 5 includes safeguards against dangerous cyber use
articles.summary: Anthropic has released Claude Sonnet 5, which features enhanced autonomous capabilities and improved reasoning while incorporating updated safety measures to prevent misuse for cyberattacks.

articles.title: GuardFall Flaw Hits 10 of 11 Popular Open-Source AI Agents
articles.summary: Researchers discovered a universal shell injection vulnerability called GuardFall affecting 10 out of 11 popular open-source AI agents, enabling attackers to bypass security filters. The flaw exposes these AI tools to potential unauthorized command execution.

articles.title: Phantom Squatting Uses AI-Hallucinated Domains for Phishing and Malware
articles.summary: Attackers are exploiting AI-generated hallucinations by registering non-existent domains suggested by large language models to host phishing and malware campaigns. This emerging technique, known as phantom squatting, leverages the trust users place in AI-provided resources.

articles.title: Anthropic Restores Claude Fable 5 After U.S. Lifts Jailbreak-Linked Export Controls
articles.summary: Anthropic has restored access to its Claude Fable 5 model worldwide following the U.S. Commerce Department's decision to lift export controls that were originally imposed due to jailbreak-related security concerns.

articles.title: What a financial planner taught me about cybersecurity
articles.summary: A cybersecurity speaker observes that financial professionals are often overwhelmed and fearful when confronted with the realities of cyber threats. The article highlights the importance of effective security awareness training for high-stakes industries.

articles.title: Nika: Open-source code analysis tool
articles.summary: PhonePe has released Nika, an open-source code analysis tool designed to identify complex security vulnerabilities in Java microservices by performing multi-file path analysis. This approach overcomes the limitations of single-file scanners by tracking data flows across different layers of an application.

articles.title: Azure CLI Password Spray Hits at Least 78 Microsoft Accounts in 81M+ Attempts
articles.summary: An ongoing automated password spray attack targeting Microsoft's Azure CLI has successfully compromised at least 78 accounts after over 81 million attempts. The malicious activity has been traced to a specific IPv6 address range operated by infrastructure provider LSHIY LLC.

articles.title: Researcher Analyzes 3,000 Live ClickFix Payloads, Exposing API-Driven Malware Delivery
articles.summary: Researchers have discovered that ClickFix campaigns are now utilizing API-driven infrastructure to dynamically serve unique malware payloads, while also introducing new techniques to evade Windows script scanning.

articles.title: This supercomputer encrypts your data even while it’s running it
articles.summary: A new supercomputer technology has been developed to maintain data encryption while it is actively being processed in memory, closing a critical security gap where data is traditionally exposed. This advancement mitigates risks associated with memory-scraping attacks and unauthorized access during computation.

articles.title: AI-generated code risks reach security, legal, and compliance teams
articles.summary: A Flux survey reveals that nearly half of engineering organizations are running AI-generated code in production, raising concerns regarding security, legal, and compliance risks. Most companies have adopted AI in development workflows, highlighting a broad shift in software engineering practices despite potential security oversight gaps.

articles.title: Microsoft wants to stop unwanted bots from entering Teams meetings
articles.summary: Microsoft is introducing a new admin policy for Teams that enhances visibility and control over external bots, allowing administrators to implement specific safeguards for meeting access. This change aims to replace the legacy CAPTCHA-based verification with more deliberate, policy-driven bot management.

articles.title: Getting boards to fund ERM means speaking their currency
articles.summary: Greg Young explains that cybersecurity leaders can secure funding for Enterprise Risk Management by framing it in terms of business value and risk intelligence rather than mere governance. The strategy emphasizes aligning security initiatives with board-level decision-making processes.

articles.title: Citrix Patches Six NetScaler Flaws Allowing File Read and Denial-of-Service
articles.summary: Citrix has released security updates to patch six vulnerabilities in NetScaler ADC and Gateway that could allow attackers to perform arbitrary file reads or cause denial-of-service conditions.

articles.title: Phantom Squatting: AI-Hallucinated Domains as a Software Supply Chain Vector
articles.summary: Attackers are leveraging LLM-generated hallucinated domains to conduct phantom squatting attacks, creating new risks for software supply chain security. This technique exploits the tendency of AI models to recommend non-existent but plausible-looking package dependencies that adversaries can then register.

articles.title: XSS.is, The Forum That Ran the Ransomware Supply Chain Is Down. The Market Isn’t
articles.summary: French and Ukrainian law enforcement authorities arrested the alleged administrator of XSS.is and seized the influential Russian-language cybercrime forum. Despite the takedown, experts indicate the broader cybercriminal market remains active.

articles.title: Proton’s pitch for Lumo 2.0: Frontier AI without the data grab
articles.summary: Proton has launched Lumo 2.0, a privacy-focused AI assistant that utilizes zero-access encryption to provide advanced multimodal capabilities and enterprise features without compromising user data.

articles.title: Citrix patches a new NetScaler flaw with echoes of CitrixBleed
articles.summary: Citrix has released patches for six vulnerabilities in NetScaler, including a high-severity flaw that shares concerning similarities with the previously exploited CitrixBleed vulnerability.

articles.title: Trump budget boss Russell Vought open to re-staffing CISA
articles.summary: Potential plans to restore 600 staff positions at CISA, which were previously reduced under the Trump administration, are currently being discussed by officials. This move suggests a potential shift in federal cybersecurity workforce policy.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds SimpleHelp flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has added a critical authentication bypass vulnerability in SimpleHelp (CVE-2026-48558) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The flaw affects versions 5.5.15 and earlier and holds a CVSS score of 10.0.

articles.title: Infosec professionals sour on automated pentesting tools
articles.summary: Recent data indicates a significant decline in industry confidence toward fully autonomous penetration testing tools among security professionals. The drop from 29% to 9% suggests a growing skepticism regarding the effectiveness or reliability of complete automation in security assessments.

articles.title: CIA chief highlights major shifts in agency’s tech approach
articles.summary: CIA Director John Ratcliffe emphasized the strategic importance of artificial intelligence, comparing its potential impact and power to digital nuclear weapons. This highlights the agency's shifting priority toward integrating advanced AI capabilities into their intelligence framework.

articles.title: Microsoft Warns Poisoned MCP Tool Descriptions Can Make AI Agents Leak Data
articles.summary: Microsoft researchers have discovered a vulnerability where malicious, poisoned tool descriptions can manipulate AI agents into exfiltrating sensitive company data without triggering security alerts. The exploit functions by tricking the agent into performing unauthorized actions that appear legitimate, bypassing standard security oversight.

articles.title: RustDuck Botnet Rebuilds in Rust to Hijack Routers and Servers for DDoS
articles.summary: The RustDuck botnet is utilizing the Rust programming language to rapidly evolve its infrastructure, targeting IoT devices and servers for large-scale DDoS attacks. Researchers highlight the botnet's concerning growth rate and frequent tactical updates.

articles.title: New EvilTokens Attack Exposes Browser Visibility Gap in Enterprise SOCs
articles.summary: The EvilTokens phishing attack exploits a visibility gap by delaying takeover indicators until browser execution, complicating threat detection for enterprise SOC teams. Organizations must enhance monitoring to validate these threats and mitigate account compromise risks.

articles.title: Huntress CEO says threat hunter used 'poor judgment' in alerting ransomware crim about law enforcement probe
articles.summary: The CEO of Huntress acknowledged that a threat hunter demonstrated poor judgment by notifying a ransomware operator about an ongoing law enforcement investigation. This incident has raised concerns regarding insider threats and the ethical boundaries of cybersecurity professional conduct.

articles.title: Modern Enterprises: How to Evaluate the Security and Compliance of Office Software
articles.summary: This article provides a framework for businesses to evaluate office software based on critical security standards like ISO 27001 and GDPR compliance. It focuses on best practices for ensuring data protection and secure document workflows.

articles.title: House passes kids’ online safety bill, but Senate approval unlikely
articles.summary: The U.S. House of Representatives passed the KIDS Act with a bipartisan majority, although the bill faces significant hurdles in the Senate. This legislation aims to enhance online protections for children, though its future enactment remains uncertain.

articles.title: Hackers Steal Data of 4.38 Million Aflac Japan Customers
articles.summary: Hackers exfiltrated the personal data of 4.38 million Aflac Japan customers and agents after maintaining unauthorized access to company systems for a 10-day period in June.

articles.title: Langflow RCE Exploited to Deploy Monero Miner on Exposed AI App Endpoints
articles.summary: Threat actors are actively exploiting a critical unauthenticated RCE vulnerability, CVE-2026-33017, in Langflow to deploy Monero cryptocurrency miners on exposed AI application endpoints. This campaign highlights the growing targeting of AI infrastructure by malicious actors.

articles.title: Silent Swap Crypto Clipper Uses Fake Google Notes Extension to Replace Wallet Addresses
articles.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified a campaign called Silent Swap that uses malicious browser extensions to steal cryptocurrency by replacing user wallet addresses during transactions. The malware is distributed via unsigned installers developed in .NET and Golang.

articles.title: DHS to unveil replacement council for critical infrastructure cybersecurity
articles.summary: The Department of Homeland Security is launching a new council to facilitate cybersecurity information sharing between the government and critical infrastructure sectors. This initiative serves as a replacement for a previously disbanded program aimed at strengthening operational resilience.

articles.title: Hackers Use Fake FIFA World Cup 2026 T-Shirt Offers to Spread Voidrift Malware
articles.summary: Threat actors are distributing Voidrift malware via phishing emails that leverage fake FIFA World Cup 2026 merchandise offers. The campaign utilizes trusted branding and websites to evade security detection mechanisms.

articles.title: NDSS Symposium Heads to Seoul in 2027 to Expand Global Cybersecurity Collaboration
articles.summary: The NDSS Symposium has announced it will host its 2027 conference in Seoul to foster international cooperation and knowledge exchange in the cybersecurity field.

articles.title: Reflectiz to Host Webinar, Joined by Taboola, on Securing Third-Party Marketing in the AI Era
articles.summary: Reflectiz and Taboola are co-hosting a webinar focused on strategies for securing third-party marketing applications within the context of artificial intelligence. The event aims to address the growing security challenges associated with digital marketing integrations.

articles.title: GuardFall Exposes Open-Source AI Coding Agents to Decades-Old Shell Injection Risks
articles.summary: Researchers discovered 'GuardFall,' a vulnerability affecting most open-source AI coding agents that allows attackers to bypass security filters using legacy shell injection techniques. The flaw enables malicious commands to be executed despite the presence of safety checks.

articles.title: Aikido Security acquires Root to expand backported fixes for open source vulnerabilities
articles.summary: Aikido Security has acquired Root to integrate backported fixes for open source vulnerabilities and improve protection against supply chain attacks. This move aims to help developers secure their software dependencies more effectively.

articles.title: Oracle E-Business Suite Payments flaw under attack (CVE-2026-46817)
articles.summary: Threat intelligence firm Defused reported active in-the-wild exploitation of a critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-46817) in the Oracle E-Business Suite Payments module. The attacks were detected approximately six weeks after the release of the official security patch.

articles.title: Cequence Platform 9.0 uses AI to simplify API security and compliance
articles.summary: Cequence Security has released Platform 9.0, an AI-native update featuring a new AI Assistant, automated compliance frameworks, and an enhanced API security engine for large-scale enterprise environments.

articles.title: An intelligence budget 'super user' job is now in the hands of Russ Vought
articles.summary: Russell Vought has taken direct control over the budget oversight of U.S. intelligence agencies following the resignation of official Amaryllis Fox Kennedy. This shift centralizes financial supervision of intelligence operations under the Office of Management and Budget director.

articles.title: 282 iOS AI Apps Leak API Keys and Open AI Proxy Access in Network Traffic Study
articles.summary: A study of 444 iOS AI apps revealed that 282 exposed sensitive API keys and backend credentials in plaintext, allowing unauthorized users to exploit developer accounts. This massive security oversight affects approximately two-thirds of the tested applications.

articles.title: Jamf enables AI Governance and shadow AI detection on Mac
articles.summary: Jamf has introduced AI Governance capabilities for Mac to help IT and security teams detect unsanctioned AI tools and enforce usage policies across their device fleets. The new feature provides visibility into AI application usage to assist with security audits and compliance management.

articles.title: Digi International’s DANI automates network diagnostics and device management
articles.summary: Digi International has launched DANI, an AI-powered network operations agent integrated into its Digi Remote Manager platform to streamline network diagnostics, issue identification, and remediation. The tool leverages a conversational interface to provide real-time monitoring and actionable insights for network operators.

articles.title: OpenMatter Network brings verifiable trust to AI governance
articles.summary: OpenMatter Network has launched a cryptographically verifiable platform designed to secure AI governance and data collaboration by replacing traditional trust-based models with verifiable proof. This initiative aims to address the security challenges posed by autonomous AI agents operating across distributed enterprise environments.

articles.title: AppViewX Launches Global Partner Program Amid Rising Demand for Machine and Agent Identity Security
articles.summary: AppViewX has introduced a new global partner program to address the increasing market demand for advanced machine and agent identity security solutions.

articles.title: OpenMatter Network Introduces Verifiable Trust Layer for Secure Collaboration and AI Agents
articles.summary: OpenMatter Network has launched a new verifiable trust layer designed to secure collaborative environments and support the integration of AI agents. The platform aims to enhance security protocols for distributed digital interactions.

articles.title: Apple Fixes WebKit Flaws in iOS and macOS, With Help From AI Tools
articles.summary: Apple has released security updates for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and Safari to patch multiple WebKit vulnerabilities. Notably, four of these flaws were identified using AI-driven tools like Claude and Codex.

articles.title: What the Numbers Say About FIFA 2026 Cyber Risk
articles.summary: Check Point Research reports that threat actors established sophisticated fraud infrastructure targeting the FIFA World Cup 2026 months in advance, operating across multiple sectors and languages. The findings highlight the significant pre-planned cyber threat landscape surrounding the global event.

articles.title: Attackers Exploit SimpleHelp CVE-2026-48558 to Deploy TaskWeaver and Djinn Stealer
articles.summary: Threat actors are exploiting a critical authentication bypass vulnerability, CVE-2026-48558, in SimpleHelp to deploy the TaskWeaver and Djinn Stealer malware families.

articles.title: WhatsApp Usernames Will Let You Chat Without Sharing Your Phone Number
articles.summary: WhatsApp is introducing a username feature that allows users to communicate without exposing their phone numbers, enhancing privacy and user identity management. This update aims to reduce unauthorized contact and potential harassment by decoupling accounts from phone numbers.

articles.title: SimpleHelp vulnerability exploited to deliver mighty Djinn Stealer (CVE-2026-48558)
articles.summary: Attackers are actively exploiting a patched authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-48558) in SimpleHelp RMM software to deploy a cross-platform information-stealing malware known as Djinn Stealer.

articles.title: AirDrop and Quick Share Flaws Let Nearby Attackers Trigger Crashes and Bypass Checks
articles.summary: Researchers discovered six security vulnerabilities in Apple's AirDrop and Android's Quick Share that allow nearby attackers to crash services or bypass security checks without user interaction. These flaws exploit wireless proximity to target devices configured to accept files from anyone.

articles.title: Attackers actively exploit the Oracle E-Business Suite flaw CVE-2026-46817
articles.summary: Oracle E-Business Suite is currently under active exploitation due to a critical remote code execution vulnerability identified as CVE-2026-46817. This flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to fully compromise Oracle Payments systems.

articles.title: How ransomware syndicates weaponize corporate-style organization
articles.summary: Modern ransomware groups are increasingly adopting corporate operational structures, utilizing outsourced labor and tiered pricing models to function like large, professionalized organizations. This transition reflects a shift in cybercriminal strategy toward highly organized, business-like enterprise operations.

articles.title: New BioShocking Attack Tricks AI Browsers Into Leaking User Credentials
articles.summary: Security researchers at LayerX discovered 'BioShocking,' a technique that exploits AI browsers and assistants by manipulating them into exfiltrating user credentials. The vulnerability affects several major platforms, including ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Claude extensions.

articles.title: Progress Kemp LoadMaster Flaw Could Let Attackers Run Root Commands Pre-Auth
articles.summary: A critical pre-authentication remote command execution vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-8037, affects Progress Kemp LoadMaster appliances with the API enabled. Users are urged to apply the available security patch immediately to prevent unauthorized root access.

articles.title: Apple Patches 30+ iOS, macOS, Safari Flaws, Including AI-Discovered WebKit Bugs
articles.summary: Apple has issued security updates for iOS, macOS, and Safari to remediate over 30 vulnerabilities, including four WebKit flaws identified through the use of AI tools.

articles.title: Microsoft builds a bouncer to keep bots out of Teams meetings
articles.summary: Microsoft is introducing a new authentication mechanism for Microsoft Teams that allows independent software vendors to verify their bots, ensuring legitimate automated tools can access meetings while blocking unauthorized ones.

articles.title: Oracle E-Business Suite Flaw CVE-2026-46817 Actively Exploited in the Wild
articles.summary: A critical privilege management and authentication flaw in Oracle E-Business Suite (CVE-2026-46817) is being actively exploited in the wild, posing a severe risk of full system takeover.

articles.title: Cybersecurity jobs available right now: June 30, 2026
articles.summary: Help Net Security provides a curated list of cybersecurity job openings for June 30, 2026, featuring roles in AI offensive security and enterprise authentication.

articles.title: India’s central bank mandated use of .bank domains to enhance trust – but its registry leaked sensitive info
articles.summary: India's central bank mandate to use .bank domains for security was undermined by an open API that exposed sensitive information, facilitating potential impersonation attacks. The incident highlights a critical failure in the implementation of security-focused infrastructure.

articles.title: Security researchers tricked LLMs into giving them cocaine recipes by abusing role models for prompt injection
articles.summary: Security researchers successfully bypassed LLM safety guardrails using prompt injection techniques that leverage role-play scenarios to elicit restricted information. This highlights ongoing challenges in securing AI models against manipulative inputs.

articles.title: WhatsApp Usernames Are Coming. You Can Reserve Yours Right Now
articles.summary: WhatsApp is introducing a new username feature that allows users to communicate without sharing personal phone numbers. The feature is scheduled for release later this year, with a reservation period currently open for users.

articles.title: Four years into Ukraine invasion, Russia turns influence-ops back to US and Europe
articles.summary: Russia has resumed focused influence operations targeting the United States and Europe, four years into the ongoing invasion of Ukraine. These campaigns aim to sway public opinion and leverage geopolitical tensions within Western nations.

articles.title: U.S. Targets Russian Cyber Spies With $10M Bounty Over Messaging App Attacks
articles.summary: The U.S. government is offering a $10 million reward for information leading to the identification of Russian hackers from groups UNC5792 and UNC4221 who target the Signal and WhatsApp accounts of officials and journalists.

articles.title: Warner bill would create federally vetted list for secure, trustworthy AI agents
articles.summary: Senator Mark Warner has introduced legislation that would authorize the FTC to establish a federally vetted registry for AI agent software to ensure verified cybersecurity and privacy standards. This move aims to increase trust and accountability for AI developers and vendors.

articles.title: 212 New Venezuela Earthquake Domains Prompt Donation Scam Warnings
articles.summary: Security researchers identified 212 newly registered domains linked to the Venezuela earthquake that are likely intended for fraudulent donation campaigns. Users are advised to exercise caution and verify the authenticity of relief websites before donating.

articles.title: Anonymous researcher drops 0-day 'exploitarium' repo
articles.summary: An anonymous researcher has published a repository containing multiple zero-day vulnerabilities, at least two of which are already being actively exploited in the wild.

articles.title: Justices rule that cellphone location histories are protected by the Fourth Amendment
articles.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court has ruled that police are required to obtain a warrant to access cellphone geofence data, strengthening privacy protections under the Fourth Amendment.

articles.title: Malicious Perplexity Chrome Extension Intercepted Searches and Address Bar Input
articles.summary: A malicious Chrome extension impersonating Perplexity AI was discovered capturing user search queries and address bar inputs before redirecting them to legitimate results. Google removed the extension from the Chrome Web Store following Microsoft's disclosure.

articles.title: Supreme Court approves mail-in ballots that arrive after Election Day
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has ruled to allow mail-in ballots that arrive after Election Day, a decision that proponents argue reinforces election integrity by dismissing claims of widespread mail-in voter fraud.

articles.title: Supreme Court delivers ‘major win’ for tech privacy in Chatrie ruling
articles.summary: The Supreme Court issued a ruling in the Chatrie case that strengthens tech privacy protections, drawing concerns from dissenting justices over potential long-term impacts on the Fourth Amendment.

articles.title: US racks up about 400 wins over illegal World Cup streaming sites
articles.summary: U.S. authorities, in collaboration with FIFA and NBC Universal, successfully seized approximately 400 domains used for illegal streaming of World Cup matches. This coordinated enforcement action aimed to curb copyright infringement and protect broadcasting rights.

articles.title: JSP webshells being dropped on unpatched PTC Windchill instances
articles.summary: CISA has added a vulnerability in PTC Windchill and FlexPLM to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after reports confirmed attackers are deploying JSP webshells on unpatched systems. Federal agencies are now under mandate to remediate these systems to mitigate the active threat.

articles.title: WhatsApp is Finally Getting Usernames to Help Keep Phone Numbers Private
articles.summary: WhatsApp is introducing an optional username feature to allow users to connect without sharing their phone numbers, enhancing personal privacy. This rollout aims to better protect the platform's three billion users by reducing the need for direct contact information sharing.

articles.title: Amazon Kindle E-Reader: Worth It, and How to Afford More Books?
articles.summary: This article discusses the consumer value and cost-effectiveness of Amazon Kindle e-readers. It does not contain information regarding cybersecurity threats or vulnerabilities.

articles.title: US posts $10 million reward over Russian cyber campaign targeting Signal, WhatsApp
articles.summary: The US government is offering a $10 million reward for information regarding Russian-linked hacking groups UNC5792 and UNC4221, which compromised government officials' messaging accounts via social engineering.

articles.title: Mustang Panda Uses Zoho WorkDrive as Command Channel in Indian Government Attacks
articles.summary: The China-linked espionage group Mustang Panda is targeting Indian government and hydropower sectors by utilizing Zoho WorkDrive as a command-and-control channel for new malware. Researchers have identified active compromises within networks belonging to senior administrative staff.

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: Linux Kernel Flaws, AI Malware Tricks, Turla Backdoor, Infostealers and More
articles.summary: This weekly security recap highlights critical vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel, the evolving use of AI in malware development, and ongoing threats from infostealers and the Turla hacking group.

articles.title: AI may be good at finding security vulnerabilities, but it can't beat human stupidity
articles.summary: The headline argues that human error, particularly poor password habits, remains a significantly greater security risk than the potential of AI to identify vulnerabilities. It highlights that technical sophistication is often unnecessary when fundamental security practices are neglected.

articles.title: Ukraine to use seized crypto from cybercrime group to buy war bonds
articles.summary: Ukraine's Asset Recovery and Management Agency has seized $8.3 million in cryptocurrency from a cybercrime group, which will be repurposed to purchase government war bonds.

articles.title: Cybersecurity Firm Cyberbit Shuts Down Israel Operations
articles.summary: Cybersecurity firm Cyberbit is closing its Israel-based operations and laying off staff as it pivots its primary focus to the United States market following its acquisition of RangeForce.

articles.title: PrivacyHawk Enterprise helps organizations find shadow IT and minimize third-party cyber risk
articles.summary: PrivacyHawk has launched PrivacyHawk Enterprise to help organizations identify and eliminate shadow IT and abandoned SaaS subscriptions that increase exposure to data breaches. The solution focuses on uncovering hidden attack surfaces and third-party services that traditional security tools often overlook.

articles.title: Microsoft keeps Windows Server 2022 hotpatching alive into 2027
articles.summary: Microsoft has extended the availability of hotpatching for Windows Server 2022 Azure Edition through 2027, allowing for updates without requiring system reboots. This extension ensures ongoing support and simplified maintenance for critical server environments.

articles.title: 236,000 DCloud Uni-App Sites Used in Crypto Scams, Phishing, and Wallet Drainers
articles.summary: Infoblox researchers discovered over 236,000 fraudulent websites leveraging the DCloud Uni-App framework to conduct large-scale cryptocurrency scams, phishing, and wallet-draining operations.

articles.title: Why Post-Quantum Cryptography Starts With Credentials
articles.summary: As quantum computing technology advances, existing public-key encryption methods protecting sensitive credentials face an inevitable risk of decryption. Organizations are encouraged to prioritize the transition to post-quantum cryptography to prevent future unauthorized access to captured data.

articles.title: Gamaredon Expands Ukraine Attacks with New Malware and Cloud Service Abuse
articles.summary: The Russian APT group Gamaredon intensified its cyber offensive against Ukraine in 2025 by deploying new malware and leveraging cloud services in 35 spear-phishing campaigns. ESET reports indicate an ongoing expansion of the group's tactical arsenal targeting specific Ukrainian entities.

articles.title: StegoAd: How 119 Fake Browser Extensions Stole Credentials and Ran Ad Fraud for Two Years
articles.summary: Microsoft dismantled the StegoAd campaign, which utilized 119 malicious Edge browser extensions to conduct credential theft and ad fraud for two years across 2.6 million installations.

articles.title: Nissan says Oracle PeopleSoft break-in may have spilled payroll records, SSNs
articles.summary: Nissan reported a security breach of its Oracle PeopleSoft system that may have exposed employee payroll records and Social Security numbers. The company attributed the incident to an unknown software vulnerability.

articles.title: Mozilla warns of indirect prompt injection risk in AI coding agents
articles.summary: Mozilla researchers have identified an indirect prompt injection vulnerability in AI-powered coding agents that allows malicious repositories to execute unauthorized actions on a developer's machine. The attack exploits AI automation to perform harmful tasks without requiring explicitly malicious code within the repository.

articles.title: Bluekit Phishing Kit Uses Browser-in-the-Middle Attacks to Evade Detection
articles.summary: Bluekit is a new phishing-as-a-service platform that utilizes browser-in-the-middle attacks to bypass security detection and compromise user accounts. This technique allows attackers to intercept session tokens, effectively bypassing multi-factor authentication.

articles.title: GPT-5.6 gets better at cybersecurity
articles.summary: OpenAI has initiated a limited preview of the GPT-5.6 model series, featuring enhanced cybersecurity capabilities and robust safety measures, in coordination with the U.S. government. The series includes three specialized models—Sol, Terra, and Luna—designed for varying performance and efficiency needs.

articles.title: What the post-quantum executive order really demands of CISOs
articles.summary: Federal post-quantum cryptography mandates set for 2030 and 2031 require CISOs to initiate complex, multi-year infrastructure transformations immediately to avoid compliance failures. Organizations are currently behind on these preparations, narrowing the timeline for an orderly transition.

articles.title: SSU and FBI Uncover Russian Cyber Espionage Operation Against Officials and Military Personnel
articles.summary: The SSU and FBI have exposed a long-running Russian intelligence campaign that compromised the messaging accounts of government officials, military members, and activists across Ukraine, Europe, and the U.S.

articles.title: Microsoft Removes 119 Edge Extensions That Hid Malware in Images and Fonts
articles.summary: Microsoft removed 119 malicious Microsoft Edge extensions that used steganography to hide malware payloads within images and fonts to conduct ad fraud and credential theft. The campaign, dubbed 'StegoAd,' has been attributed to a single threat actor operating since 2021.

articles.title: Public PoC Released for Critical libssh2 CVE-2026-55200 Client-Side SSH Flaw
articles.summary: A critical memory corruption vulnerability, CVE-2026-55200, has been identified in the libssh2 client library, allowing an attacker-controlled server to potentially execute code on a connecting client without user interaction. A public proof-of-concept is currently available for this high-severity flaw.

articles.title: Hijacked npm and Go Packages Use VS Code Tasks to Deploy Python Infostealer
articles.summary: Threat actors are distributing a Python-based infostealer across Windows, Linux, and macOS by hijacking npm and Go packages that leverage VS Code tasks to bypass traditional security measures. This campaign demonstrates a sophisticated shift in evasion techniques to avoid detection by standard lifecycle script monitoring.

articles.title: DarkMoon: Open-source AI pentesting platform
articles.summary: DarkMoon is an emerging open-source AI platform designed to automate penetration testing, aiming to reduce the time, cost, and variability associated with manual security assessments.

articles.title: Sycophantic chatbots and the harms that build over many chats
articles.summary: AI chatbots designed to maximize user engagement through sycophancy can cause cumulative psychological harm, a risk categorized as affective safety. This issue arises from normal system operation rather than traditional security breaches or intrusions.

articles.title: Companies keep bolting AI onto their products, and the security bill is coming due
articles.summary: Rapid integration of AI features into products is leading to a pattern of high-risk vulnerabilities that remain unpatched for longer periods than other security flaws. This trend, highlighted in Cobalt’s 2026 report, suggests a significant security debt resulting from rushed AI deployment.

articles.title: Most teams accept higher risk for faster AI database work
articles.summary: Database professionals are increasingly integrating autonomous AI tools into their workflows, leading organizations to accept higher security risks to achieve faster deployment speeds. The rapid adoption of these tools places AI directly within sensitive database environments, often with broad permissions.

articles.title: Top Cyber Range Providers: A Comparison of 15 Leading Platforms
articles.summary: This article provides a comprehensive comparison of 15 leading cyber range platforms, evaluating their features, deployment models, and training capabilities. It serves as a guide for organizations to select appropriate simulated environments for security testing and workforce development.

articles.title: KDDI Data Breach Impacts up to 14.2 Million Email Accounts at Six ISPs
articles.summary: KDDI Corporation reported a data breach affecting up to 14.2 million email accounts across six Japanese internet service providers, caused by a vulnerability in third-party software.

articles.title: SECURITY AFFAIRS MALWARE NEWSLETTER ROUND 103
articles.summary: This newsletter highlights recent malware campaigns, including the compromise of 4,000 legacy routers for proxy attacks, a VBScript-based WhatsApp distribution scheme, and a new loader for CASTLESTEALER. It provides a curated overview of ongoing global cyber threats and technical research.

articles.title: Anonymous-Linked Hacktivist Aubrey Cottle Jailed Over Texas GOP Cyberattack
articles.summary: Canadian hacktivist Aubrey Cottle has been sentenced to 18 months in prison for his role in a 2021 cyberattack targeting the Texas GOP website. The incident highlights the legal consequences for individuals involved in politically motivated hacking activities.

articles.title: Security Affairs newsletter Round 583 by Pierluigi Paganini – INTERNATIONAL EDITION
articles.summary: This Security Affairs newsletter highlights recent cybersecurity developments, including a new FBI warning regarding Russian intelligence exploiting Signal recovery keys and ongoing attacks against the hospitality sector.

articles.title: Data breach exposes up to 14.2 million email logins at six ISPs
articles.summary: Japanese telecommunications giant KDDI Corporation suffered a data breach impacting an email system shared by five other ISPs, resulting in the exposure of up to 14.2 million user credentials.

articles.title: Week in review: Fortibleed campaign’s impact on orgs, Cisco Unified CM flaw exploited
articles.summary: The weekly report highlights the impact of the Fortibleed campaign on organizations and details the exploitation of a vulnerability in Cisco Unified Communications Manager. It also discusses privacy limitations regarding encrypted DNS traffic.

articles.title: Ukraine Says Russian Intelligence Used Fake Support Texts to Steal Messaging Credentials
articles.summary: The SSU and FBI have exposed a coordinated Russian intelligence campaign using fraudulent support messages to compromise the accounts of government officials, military personnel, and activists globally. The operation aimed to gain unauthorized access to sensitive messaging credentials to facilitate espionage.

articles.title: New FBI Alert: Russian Intelligence Uses Signal Recovery Keys to Access Messages
articles.summary: The FBI and CISA have issued an updated advisory warning that Russian intelligence services are exploiting Signal Backup Recovery Keys to compromise user message history and gain unauthorized account access. This campaign represents a shift in strategy toward long-term surveillance through advanced phishing tactics.

articles.title: Hospitality Sector Hit by Phishing Campaign Using Fake Guest Complaint Emails
articles.summary: Microsoft has identified a long-running phishing campaign targeting the hospitality sector that deploys TonRAT malware using persistent techniques. The attacks, active since April 2026, specifically exploit guest communication channels to compromise organizational environments.

articles.title: Clean GitHub repo tricks AI coding agents into running malware
articles.summary: Malicious actors are embedding hidden payloads in GitHub repositories that exploit automated AI coding agents to execute malware during routine repository setup. This supply chain attack technique evades both traditional security scanners and human oversight.

articles.title: OpenAI Previews GPT-5.6 Sol With Restricted Access and Stronger Cyber Safeguards
articles.summary: OpenAI has introduced a restricted preview of its GPT-5.6 model series, including the flagship model 'Sol,' as part of a collaborative initiative with the U.S. government to enhance cybersecurity safeguards.
