articles.title: DirtyClone: Fourth Linux Kernel Flaw in Six Weeks Escalates to Root

It focuses on features like incremental scanning, automated ownership, and custom rule management.

articles.summary: Researchers have identified a new malware family named SharkLoader, which is being utilized in the StrikeShark campaign to deploy Cobalt Strike Beacons against government and diplomatic targets. articles.summary: Threat actors are impersonating legitimate organizations through fraudulent OpenAI invites to harvest sensitive corporate information from employees. This social engineering campaign exploits trust in AI platforms to gain unauthorized access to internal data.

articles.summary: Chinese-speaking threat actor CL-STA-1062 is conducting persistent cyber espionage operations targeting critical infrastructure in Southeast Asia using custom malware and a new backdoor dubbed TinyRCT.

articles.summary: A Chinese-speaking APT actor identified as CL-STA-1062 is targeting Southeast Asian government and energy entities using a new custom backdoor named TinyRCT. The campaign represents a focused effort against critical infrastructure in the region.

articles.summary: This article explores the implementation of an AI-driven GRC agent designed to automate control monitoring, evidence gap identification, and remediation task management for compliance professionals.

articles.summary: A critical local privilege escalation vulnerability in the Linux kernel's traffic-control subsystem allows unprivileged users to gain root access via an out-of-bounds write. articles.summary: A high-severity vulnerability in Amazon Q Developer allowed attackers to execute arbitrary code and steal cloud credentials by exploiting the application's handling of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. Amazon has since released a patch to address the security flaw.

articles.summary: Apple removed several major Russian applications, including VKontakte, from its App Store, prompting accusations of political censorship from the Russian government.

articles.summary: The Ukrainian Security Service reported that Russian operatives successfully compromised high-profile messaging accounts by masquerading as technical support staff to steal user credentials. articles.summary: A macOS XPC vulnerability allowed unprivileged users to disable security software like CrowdStrike and Kandji. The vendors have since released patches to address the issue discovered by XM Cyber.

articles.summary: CISA has added a critical remote code execution vulnerability in PTC Windchill software to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog due to ongoing active exploitation. The flaw is being leveraged by attackers to deploy web shells.

articles.summary: The Miasma supply chain attack has compromised over 20 npm packages, including Leo Platform and RStreams, to steal developer credentials and target software maintainers. articles.summary: The FCC has approved stricter regulations for undersea cable infrastructure, including a new requirement for submarine line terminal equipment operators to obtain licenses. This initiative aims to strengthen the security and oversight of critical telecommunications infrastructure.

articles.summary: Proof has introduced x401, an open and issuer-neutral protocol designed to verify the identity and authorization of AI agents interacting with websites and APIs. articles.summary: The DirtyClone Linux kernel vulnerability allows local attackers to achieve root-level privilege escalation by corrupting file-backed memory through cloned network packets. Identified as CVE-2026-43503, the flaw has a CVSS score of 8.8 and is part of the DirtyFrag family.

articles.title: Critical open-source projects get a new security framework
articles.summary: The Linux Foundation has launched Akrites, a new industry initiative designed to streamline the remediation and disclosure process for vulnerabilities in critical open-source software. This framework addresses the increased risk posed by AI-accelerated exploitation timelines.

articles.title: Guardian Agents: The Next Layer of Identity Governance
articles.summary: The rapid integration of autonomous AI agents in enterprise environments is creating significant security gaps, as traditional identity governance frameworks are ill-equipped to manage machine-speed access. The headline highlights the urgent need for new governance structures to oversee these non-human actors.

articles.title: Activist Phone Hacked With Cellebrite After Russia Contract Cancellation
articles.summary: Russian authorities utilized Cellebrite forensic tools to bypass security measures on an activist's confiscated iPhone 12, despite the company's prior public commitment to terminate contracts with the country. This incident highlights ongoing concerns regarding the potential for forensic software misuse against political targets.

articles.title: Miasma Malware Targets npm Packages and GitHub Actions in Supply Chain Attack
articles.summary: The Miasma malware family has expanded its supply chain attack campaign to compromise additional npm packages and GitHub Actions, while also extending its reach into the Go ecosystem.

articles.summary: Synology has released a critical security update for its MailPlus Server to address three vulnerabilities that could allow remote attackers to conduct unauthorized file operations, access internal services, and trigger denial-of-service attacks. articles.title: U.S. CISA adds Cisco and PTC Windchill and FlexPLM flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog to include critical flaws affecting Cisco, PTC Windchill, and FlexPLM products. Organizations are urged to address these vulnerabilities to mitigate the risk of exploitation.

articles.summary: A 2026 report by Black Kite reveals that ransomware attacks against European organizations are rising, with threat actors increasingly targeting supply chains as their primary entry point. articles.summary: The team behind Coinspaid Solutions has rebranded as Coinspaid Dev to focus on positioning themselves as a prominent voice in blockchain infrastructure engineering.

articles.title: Microsoft Warns of Photo ZIP Phishing Campaign Targeting Hotels with Node.js Implant
articles.summary: Microsoft is tracking an ongoing phishing campaign targeting hospitality organizations across Europe and Asia that uses malicious ZIP files to deploy a Node.js implant. articles.summary: Fortra researchers have identified Mirage2FA, a sophisticated phishing kit that uses HTML smuggling and obfuscated JavaScript to bypass security filters and steal Microsoft 365 credentials during MFA processes. The campaign utilizes business-themed lures like fake invoices and payment requests to target users via email.

articles.summary: Polymarket experienced a security breach after attackers compromised a third-party vendor to inject malicious code into its website, resulting in the theft of $2.94 million in user funds.

articles.summary: Polish authorities, in collaboration with the FBI and HSI, dismantled an international cybercrime gang responsible for SIM-swapping attacks, cryptocurrency theft, and money laundering. articles.summary: ZeroTier has released the second release candidate for its quantum-secure networking platform, aligning with upcoming U.S. government post-quantum cryptography standards. This move aims to protect network traffic against future threats posed by advanced quantum computing.

articles.summary: ThreatModeler has launched Nexus, an agentic threat modeling platform that leverages AI governance to automate security architecture analysis throughout the software development lifecycle.

articles.summary: North Korean threat actors have developed a Rust-based macOS implant called macOS.Gaslight that utilizes prompt injection payloads to deceive AI-driven security analysis tools. articles.title: Google Details Turla's New STOCKSTAY Backdoor Used in Ukraine Espionage Attacks
articles.summary: Google Threat Intelligence has identified a new .NET backdoor named STOCKSTAY, developed by the Russian-linked threat actor Turla for use in espionage operations against Ukrainian government and military entities. articles.summary: The threat actor group CL-STA-1062 is conducting espionage operations against Southeast Asian government agencies and critical infrastructure using a hybrid toolkit featuring the custom TinyRCT backdoor.

articles.summary: Upwind Security has launched an AI-powered sensor that integrates endpoint activity with cloud security data to improve visibility into AI-related risks and developer activities. The platform aims to unify security monitoring across both cloud environments and endpoint devices.

articles.summary: A popular Chrome extension with over 10 million installs, 'Adblock for YouTube', was found to contain a dormant script injection capability that allows for arbitrary JavaScript execution. articles.summary: Checksum has released an API Agent designed to automatically generate and maintain stateful, journey-based tests for backend APIs to ensure testing keeps pace with rapid code development. articles.summary: Reco has launched Reco Agent Security to help organizations manage the risks of autonomous AI agents, including data exposure and unauthorized process disruption across enterprise ecosystems. articles.summary: Mitiga has launched Agentic Runtime Security, a platform designed to provide automated detection and response across cloud, SaaS, identity, and AI environments. articles.summary: Veritone has launched Veritone Assess, an AI-powered tool designed to help public sector agencies streamline evidence analysis and automate compliance reviews for complex datasets. articles.title: ThreatsDay Bulletin: Smart TV Proxyware, 24-Year curl Bug, AI Crime Forums + 13 More Stories
articles.summary: This bulletin covers a diverse range of cybersecurity issues, including smart TV proxyware, a long-standing curl vulnerability, and the rise of AI-driven cybercrime forums. articles.title: runZero 5.0 unifies exposure management to accelerate risk reduction

articles.title: Ukraine's state postal operator reports app disruption after cyberattack

articles.summary: Stellar Cyber has updated its security platform to versions 6.5 and 6.6, introducing AI-driven workflows, enhanced threat detection, and improved data onboarding capabilities. articles.summary: Microsoft and international law enforcement agencies collaborated to disrupt the infrastructure of three cybercrime-as-a-service operations. The initiative targeted over 300 servers, aiming to dismantle the underlying supply chain of malware distribution.

articles.summary: Mandiant identified that malicious actors exploited a Cisco zero-day vulnerability to obtain root-level access within a communications service provider's network. The full extent of the intrusion and the identity of the attackers remain under investigation.

articles.title: Europol Disrupts StealC and Amadey Malware Infrastructure in Operation Endgame
articles.summary: Europol led a multi-national law enforcement operation, titled 'Operation Endgame', to successfully dismantle the command-and-control infrastructure of the widespread StealC and Amadey malware families.

articles.summary: Microsoft leveraged AI to identify and connect the StealC and Amadey malware operations, leading to a legal action that resulted in the shutdown of over 200 command-and-control servers.

articles.summary: CISA has issued an alert regarding the active exploitation of a critical code injection vulnerability (CVE-2025-67038) in Lantronix EDS5000 Series devices. Federal agencies are mandated to implement security patches by June 26, 2026.

articles.title: Amadey and StealC Malware Network Disrupted, 27M Stolen Credentials Recovered
articles.summary: Law enforcement agencies and private tech partners collaborated to dismantle the command-and-control infrastructure of the Amadey and StealC botnets, successfully recovering 27 million stolen credentials. This operation aimed to cripple the distribution networks used for ransomware, fraud, and attacks on critical infrastructure.

articles.title: New GhostShell Hacking Group Targets Ukraine’s Drone Defense Sector
articles.summary: The GhostShell hacking group is conducting a cyber espionage campaign against Ukraine's drone defense sector by distributing malicious files disguised as official drone documentation to exfiltrate sensitive credentials. The attack leverages social engineering tactics to compromise defense personnel and gain access to classified information.

articles.title: Law enforcement hits StealC and Amadey malware networks
articles.summary: International law enforcement, supported by private sector partners, successfully dismantled the infrastructure for the StealC and Amadey malware networks. This operation targeted the delivery mechanisms used by these criminal groups to harvest sensitive data.

articles.title: CISA warns of max severity Ubiquiti flaws exploited in attacks
articles.summary: CISA has issued a warning regarding active exploitation of critical vulnerabilities in Ubiquiti UniFi OS and Lantronix serial-to-ethernet devices. Users are advised to patch these flaws immediately to prevent potential unauthorized access.

articles.title: Amadey, StealC malware operations disrupted in Operation Endgame action
articles.summary: Microsoft and international law enforcement agencies have successfully disrupted the infrastructure supporting the Amadey and StealC malware operations under the multi-national Operation Endgame initiative.

articles.summary: Deutsche Bahn experienced a nationwide railway service disruption caused by a technical malfunction in its 2G-based GSM-R communications infrastructure. Operations have since resumed following the resolution of the outage.

articles.title: Algerian national accused of running cybercrime marketplaces extradited to US
articles.summary: An Algerian national allegedly operating online marketplaces for cybercrime tools has been extradited from Spain to the United States to face charges of bank fraud conspiracy.

articles.title: Securing the service desk: Why social engineering attacks keep succeeding
articles.summary: Service desks are increasingly targeted by attackers using social engineering to gain unauthorized access through password resets and MFA bypasses. The article outlines these tactics and provides defensive strategies for organizations to mitigate these risks.

articles.title: Anthropic’s Claude Tag gives AI agents independent identities
articles.summary: Anthropic has introduced Claude Tag, a feature that assigns AI agents independent identities and specific tool access permissions within shared workspaces. This architecture isolates AI activity from individual user credentials, effectively reducing the risk of unauthorized data exposure in team environments.

articles.title: Why Frontier AI makes prioritization the most important part of your CTEM program
articles.summary: The rapid emergence of frontier AI is expected to cause a massive surge in vulnerability disclosures, necessitating a transition toward Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM) for effective risk prioritization. Traditional vulnerability management programs are deemed inadequate to handle the accelerating volume of threats.

articles.title: Fake npm Packages Impersonate PostCSS Tool to Steal Chrome Passwords
articles.summary: Malicious npm packages disguised as the PostCSS tool are infecting Windows systems with remote access trojans to exfiltrate stored Chrome browser passwords. The campaign utilizes a staged infection process to stealthily deploy malware onto developer environments.

articles.title: Indian auto giant Bajaj Auto hit by ransomware incident
articles.summary: Indian automotive manufacturer Bajaj Auto confirmed a ransomware attack, prompting the company to implement containment measures to mitigate the incident's impact. The breach was reported via a regulatory filing shortly after its detection.

articles.title: Cisco Unified CM Flaw CVE-2026-20230 Actively Exploited in the Wild
articles.summary: Cisco Unified Communications Manager is currently being exploited in the wild via CVE-2026-20230, a high-severity vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to achieve root access through SSRF and arbitrary file writes.

articles.title: Cordyceps CI/CD Flaws Expose 300+ GitHub Repositories to Supply-Chain Attacks
articles.summary: Researchers discovered a critical CI/CD workflow vulnerability dubbed 'Cordyceps' that exposes over 300 GitHub repositories to potential supply-chain attacks. This flaw allows unauthorized actors to hijack workflows and gain full control over major organizational repositories.

articles.title: In a first, a court takedown goes after two cybercrime tools at once
articles.summary: Microsoft and its partners successfully disrupted over 200 command and control servers associated with the Amadey and StealC malware, marking the first time two cybercrime tools were taken down simultaneously via a court order.

articles.title: Phishing attack on healthcare firm Xsolis impacts 1.4 million people
articles.summary: Healthcare technology firm Xsolis confirmed that a targeted phishing attack led to unauthorized network access, affecting approximately 1.4 million individuals. The incident, which occurred in January 2026, compromised sensitive data managed by the company's AI-powered healthcare software.

articles.title: SuperOps and Guardz bundle IT operations and security into one product for MSPs
articles.summary: SuperOps and Guardz have formed a partnership to offer a unified platform for MSPs that combines IT operations, remote monitoring, and AI-driven security capabilities. This integration aims to streamline workflows by merging operational and security data into a single, bundled solution.

articles.title: London cops bring live facial recognition to West End
articles.summary: London police have implemented live facial recognition technology in the West End, drawing criticism from privacy advocates who argue it violates the principle of policing by consent.

articles.title: Cisco Unified CM flaw actively exploited to drop webshells (CVE-2026-20230)
articles.summary: Cisco Unified Communications Manager is currently being exploited in the wild via a Server-Side Request Forgery vulnerability (CVE-2026-20230) to deploy webshells and achieve remote code execution. Attackers are utilizing automated sweeps originating from Tor to target the WebDialer component and establish persistence.

articles.title: Dawn of the Apex Agentic Adversary
articles.summary: The shift toward autonomous agentic threats is ending the era of human-speed cybersecurity, necessitating a transition to real-time, automated defense mechanisms. This evolution renders traditional manual patch cycles and response timelines dangerously obsolete.

articles.title: Stealthy Mistic backdoor linked to ransomware access broker KongTuke
articles.summary: A newly discovered backdoor called Mistic is being utilized by the threat actor KongTuke to facilitate ransomware attacks against organizations in the insurance, education, and IT sectors.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds Ubiquiti UniFi OS and Lantronix EDS5000 plugin flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has added critical vulnerabilities affecting Ubiquiti UniFi OS and Lantronix EDS5000 devices to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog due to active exploitation. This mandate requires U.S. federal agencies to address these security gaps within a specified timeframe to mitigate ongoing risks.

articles.title: LastPass customer data exposed through Klue supply chain attack
articles.summary: LastPass customer data was exposed after attackers leveraged OAuth tokens compromised during a supply chain attack on the third-party platform Klue. The breach allowed unauthorized access to LastPass's Salesforce environment through integrated systems.

articles.title: FortiBleed: The Broker Who Turned 73,000 Firewalls Into a Product Catalog
articles.summary: A researcher discovered a publicly exposed server containing valid login credentials for over 73,000 Fortinet firewalls, highlighting a significant access-brokering operation. This data leak, dubbed FortiBleed, compromises the security of thousands of global organizations.

articles.title: Google Workspace expands password reset alerts to all admins
articles.summary: Google is expanding its Workspace alert system to notify administrators whenever any administrative account password is reset, enhancing visibility and security for privileged accounts. This update helps organizations more effectively monitor and respond to potential unauthorized access attempts.

articles.title: Open-source security is posing challenges governments can’t easily solve
articles.summary: The widespread and decentralized nature of open-source software, combined with insufficient corporate oversight and emerging AI threats, is creating complex security challenges that current government strategies struggle to address.

articles.title: DoJ Seizes Huione Cloud Account Tied to Cyber Scam Money Laundering
articles.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice seized a cloud computing account used by Cambodia-based Huione Group subsidiaries for laundering cyber scam proceeds. This action coincided with new U.S. Treasury sanctions targeting entities linked to the Prince Group for their role in illicit financial activities.

articles.title: One Railway Radio Outage Stopped Trains Across Germany and Nobody Knew Why
articles.summary: A nationwide GSM-R network failure in Germany forced Deutsche Bahn to halt all train operations across the country. The incident highlights critical vulnerabilities and reliability issues within aging railway communications infrastructure.

articles.title: Best Crypto Payment Solutions for E-Commerce Businesses
articles.summary: This article provides a comparative overview of cryptocurrency payment gateways and tools designed to facilitate digital currency transactions for e-commerce platforms. It focuses on the functional features of financial technology integration rather than specific security threats.

articles.title: Qodo expands platform to help teams govern AI-generated code and engineering standards
articles.summary: Qodo has introduced three new governance capabilities—Cross-Repo Code Review, Custom Rules Miner, and Skill Review Standards—to help enterprises manage the security and quality of AI-generated code. These tools aim to mitigate risks associated with the increasing autonomy of AI agents in the software development lifecycle.

articles.title: Brinqa BYOAI lets organizations use any AI platform with trusted risk data
articles.summary: Brinqa has introduced a 'Bring Your Own AI' (BYOAI) capability that allows enterprises to integrate various AI models and agents with its exposure intelligence platform. This integration ensures that AI-driven risk analysis is based on consistent, accurate, and up-to-date security data.

articles.title: Cequence introduces behavioral bot detection and biometric verification without CAPTCHAs
articles.summary: Cequence Security has launched Intent Graph and Biometric Check to provide bot defense across web, mobile, and AI traffic, eliminating the need for traditional CAPTCHAs. These new capabilities utilize behavioral architecture to detect sophisticated bots that typically bypass standard client-side signals.

articles.title: New Secure Code Warrior framework helps CISOs govern AI-driven software development
articles.summary: Secure Code Warrior has launched the SCW AI Adoption Model, a framework designed to help CISOs manage and govern the integration of AI in software development as it scales toward autonomous agentic systems. It provides guidance on necessary training and security controls based on an organization's specific level of AI adoption.

articles.title: DigiCert brings independent trust validation to confidential computing environments
articles.summary: DigiCert has partnered with Google Cloud to provide independent PKI-based cryptographic verification for confidential computing environments. This initiative aims to ensure the authenticity and integrity of sensitive cloud-hosted workloads and infrastructure.

articles.title: Cisco Unified CM Flaw Exploited After PoC Reveals File-Write Path to Root
articles.summary: Threat actors are actively exploiting a critical improper input validation vulnerability in Cisco Unified Communications Manager, designated as CVE-2026-20230, which allows for remote, unauthenticated file-write access to the root directory.

articles.title: Where IT meets OT and railway cybersecurity gets harder
articles.summary: This interview explores the cybersecurity challenges of integrating legacy operational technology with modern IT in railway systems, focusing on increased attack surfaces, regulatory compliance, and risk management. It discusses how technical teams handle patching vulnerabilities while maintaining critical service availability and addressing liability concerns.

articles.title: You have got to be KDDI-ng – Japanese telco exposes 14.2 million managed email credentials
articles.summary: Japanese telecommunications company KDDI suffered a massive data breach, exposing the managed email credentials of 14.2 million users across five different ISPs. The incident highlights significant security gaps in the management of user account information.

articles.title: Samsung KNOX Kernel UAF Exposes Millions of Galaxy Devices
articles.summary: A kernel use-after-free vulnerability (CVE-2026-20971) within Samsung's KNOX security stack allowed potential exploitation through memory corruption, affecting millions of Galaxy devices before a patch was released in January 2026.

articles.title: OpenClaw’s Skill Marketplace and the Emerging AI Supply Chain Threat
articles.summary: Unit 42 researchers identified that the ClawHub marketplace hosts malicious AI skills capable of bypassing security scanners to deliver infostealers and conduct financial fraud. This highlights an emerging supply chain threat targeting AI-integrated platforms.

articles.title: Cisco Unified CM flaw CVE-2026-20230 now exploited in attacks
articles.summary: Cisco Unified Communications Manager is under active exploitation due to a high-severity server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability designated as CVE-2026-20230.

articles.title: Tata Electronics confirms cyberattack as hackers leak data
articles.summary: Tata Electronics has confirmed a cyberattack on its IT infrastructure that resulted in the unauthorized exposure of company data. The incident is currently being investigated, with the company working to secure its systems.

articles.title: Windows 11 KB5095093 update rolls out new Point-in-Time restore feature
articles.summary: Microsoft has released the KB5095093 preview update for Windows 11, introducing a new Point-in-Time restore feature alongside various bug fixes. This update aims to enhance system recovery capabilities for users on versions 24H2 and 25H2.

articles.title: Healthtech firm Xolis suffers data breach impacting 1.4 million people
articles.summary: Healthtech firm Xsolis confirmed a data breach affecting 1.4 million individuals resulting from a successful phishing attack on their network.

articles.title: Internet Society Foundation Opens Global Call for Common Good Cyber Fund to Strengthen Cybersecurity
articles.summary: The Internet Society Foundation has launched the Common Good Cyber Fund to provide financial support for initiatives that strengthen global cybersecurity. The project aims to improve digital resilience by funding efforts that serve the public interest.

articles.title: Five Eyes agencies sound alarm about AI’s threat to cybersecurity
articles.summary: The Five Eyes intelligence alliance has issued a joint warning that artificial intelligence is rapidly escalating cybersecurity threats, with significant impacts expected within months rather than years.

articles.title: Justice Department seizes infrastructure used by cyber scam and criminal marketplace
articles.summary: The U.S. Justice Department has seized digital infrastructure linked to cyber scams and criminal marketplaces, while the Treasury Department sanctioned the Cambodian-based Huione Group for its involvement.

articles.summary: A new macOS campaign utilizes a 'ClickFix' technique to trick users into executing Terminal commands that silently download and launch info-stealing malware via malicious DMG files.

articles.summary: LastPass confirmed a security breach resulting from the compromise of a Klue OAuth token used by an unauthorized actor. The incident highlights a supply chain vulnerability affecting the password manager's customer data.

articles.summary: A Russian-speaking threat actor is conducting a massive credential-harvesting campaign dubbed FortiBleed, affecting over 430,000 global FortiGate firewall installations. The operation leverages brute-forcing and service exploitation to compromise systems for financial gain.

articles.summary: Security researchers at Mythos have uncovered a long-standing memory leak vulnerability dubbed 'Squidbleed' that has impacted legacy systems like NetWare, FTP, and HTTP since the late 1990s. The flaw represents a significant historical security oversight affecting archaic network protocols.

articles.title: Feds seize alleged cyber-scam infrastructure connected to Southeast Asian company
articles.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice seized a cloud computing account linked to subsidiaries of the Huione Group, which is already sanctioned by the U.S. government for its ties to cyber-scam operations. This action represents a targeted strike against infrastructure supporting illicit financial and fraudulent activity.

articles.summary: President Trump signed an executive order requiring federal agencies to transition to post-quantum cryptography to secure sensitive data against future quantum computing capabilities.

articles.summary: Researchers at Zafran Labs discovered four vulnerabilities, including two critical flaws, in the open-source Dify platform that potentially expose sensitive data across over one million AI applications. articles.summary: A CI/CD vulnerability dubbed 'Cordyceps' allows anonymous actors to exploit GitHub Actions workflows, potentially leading to build poisoning and the exposure of sensitive tokens in major projects. articles.summary: The emergence of AI-generated content is transforming academic fraud by enabling the creation of original-looking work and fabricated sources, necessitating new detection capabilities for educational institutions.

articles.summary: House leaders have introduced a version of the kids' online safety bill that notably excludes the 'duty of care' provision designed to force platforms to mitigate algorithmic harms. articles.summary: Security firm AIR demonstrated a significant supply chain vulnerability by successfully deploying a fake AI agent skill that bypassed all security scanners and reached 26,000 corporate and individual accounts. The experiment highlights a critical gap in the security vetting processes of popular AI agent marketplaces.

articles.summary: President Trump signed an executive order mandating that federal agencies migrate high-value systems to post-quantum cryptography by 2030 and 2031 to mitigate future quantum-computing threats. National security systems are excluded from this timeline and will follow a separate regulatory path.

articles.title: What the Fortibleed campaign means for organizations running FortiGate firewalls
articles.summary: A sophisticated, automated credential-harvesting campaign dubbed FortiBleed has compromised thousands of FortiGate firewalls by leveraging exposed attacker tools and scripts. articles.title: Algerian man charged with running two cybercrime marketplaces
articles.summary: An Algerian national, Abdellah Belmili, has been charged by federal prosecutors for allegedly operating two dark-web marketplaces that sold stolen financial credentials and phishing kits targeting U.S. banks.

articles.summary: GitHub is updating the 'actions/checkout' tool to mitigate security risks associated with 'pull_request_target' triggers, which have been exploited to execute malicious code with elevated privileges. The update aims to harden software supply chain security starting June 18, 2026.

articles.summary: N-able has introduced a new 'Shadow AI Visibility' feature across its UEM and security platforms to help IT teams track and manage unauthorized AI tool usage on endpoints and networks. This tool aims to mitigate security risks associated with the rapid and often unmonitored adoption of AI applications within corporate environments.

articles.title: The Exploit Doesn't Exist. You Can Still Prove It Works Against You
articles.summary: The article discusses how security teams can proactively validate vulnerability exploitability to defend against threats before public exploits are released. This approach helps organizations mitigate risk despite the speed at which attackers weaponize new vulnerabilities.

articles.summary: LastPass confirmed a data breach involving unauthorized access to customer data within their Salesforce environment, resulting from a supply chain attack targeting the company's OAuth tokens via Klue.

articles.title: Dragos unveils OT-native AI to help critical infrastructure teams prioritize threats faster
articles.summary: Dragos has launched EmberAI, an operational technology-native AI tool designed to help critical infrastructure teams analyze and prioritize security threats using historical and real-time intelligence. The platform aims to improve asset visibility and vulnerability management by leveraging over a decade of specialized industrial security expertise.

articles.title: Using Reddit to manipulate AI search results is surprisingly easy
articles.summary: A Cornell Tech study reveals that AI research agents can be easily manipulated by brief, targeted Reddit comments, raising significant concerns about the integrity of AI-generated reports. This vulnerability highlights the risks of AI systems relying on unverified, community-generated content from the web.

articles.title: Two Scattered Spider members plead guilty over cyberattack that crippled London transit
articles.summary: Two members of the threat group Scattered Spider have pleaded guilty to infiltrating Transport for London's network, which caused significant and long-term disruption to public transit services in 2024.

articles.title: Webinar: Why email security teams are drowning in alerts
articles.summary: The headline highlights the issue of alert fatigue in email security teams caused by the high volume of phishing and account takeover attacks. It suggests that leveraging behavioral AI for automation can improve operational efficiency and response times.

articles.title: New CryptoBandits Malware Uses USB Drives and Tor to Steal Crypto
articles.summary: Microsoft researchers have identified 'CryptoBandits,' a new malware strain that leverages USB drives and the Tor network to hijack cryptocurrency transactions by modifying wallet addresses. articles.title: Agentic AI: The Weapon That No Longer Needs a Warrior
articles.summary: The rise of agentic AI represents a paradigm shift where autonomous systems can select and engage targets without direct human intervention. This evolution fundamentally alters the nature of cyber warfare by removing the human decision-maker from the loop.

articles.title: The Evolution of iGaming Fraud: What Security Teams Should Expect in 2027
articles.summary: This article explores how emerging technologies like AI, deepfakes, and fraud-as-a-service are expected to evolve the iGaming threat landscape by 2027. It provides actionable guidance for security teams to prepare their defenses against these sophisticated future risks.

articles.summary: Scammers are setting up fraudulent websites promising early access to GTA 6 in exchange for cryptocurrency payments to deceive eager gamers. These sites are unauthorized and provide no access to the game, resulting in financial loss for victims.

articles.summary: Two teenagers associated with the Scattered Spider group have pleaded guilty to orchestrating a major cyberattack against Transport for London and various US healthcare organizations, resulting in millions of pounds of damages. articles.summary: Two members of the Scattered Spider hacker group have pleaded guilty to charges linked to a 2024 cyberattack on Transport for London that incurred £29 million in costs. The defendants face sentencing in July for their violations of the UK's Computer Misuse Act.

articles.title: Omada Identity Sovereign targets Europe’s growing digital sovereignty demands
articles.summary: Omada has launched Omada Identity Sovereign to help regulated European organizations meet strict digital sovereignty and compliance requirements for identity governance. The solution is designed to align with evolving regulatory frameworks like DORA and NIS2.

articles.title: Hack The Box adds crisis simulations and SOC training to strengthen cyber readiness
articles.summary: Hack The Box has expanded its platform with new SOC training, crisis simulations, and AI-driven tools to help organizations improve cybersecurity team readiness and operational resilience. These additions aim to help security leaders identify skill gaps and better prepare for evolving AI-based cyber threats.

articles.title: Mavenir turns NOC knowledge into automation for autonomous networks
articles.summary: Mavenir has launched an Agentic Service Assurance Framework designed to automate complex network operations across 5G and cloud-native environments using a multi-agent AI system. The platform aims to streamline fault detection and resolution without requiring the replacement of existing infrastructure.

articles.title: Malicious npm Packages Pose as PostCSS Tools to Deliver Windows RAT
articles.summary: Researchers discovered malicious npm packages masquerading as PostCSS tools to infect Windows systems with a remote access trojan. The packages were recently published and have recorded several hundred downloads.

articles.title: OpenAI wants AI to fix vulnerabilities, not just find them
articles.summary: OpenAI has expanded its Daybreak initiative to integrate AI models and security tools designed to not only identify software vulnerabilities but also facilitate their automated remediation. This effort aims to alleviate industry pressure by streamlining the patching process for developers and security teams.

articles.title: F5 launches AI Security Platform to uncover and secure shadow AI
articles.summary: F5 has launched an AI Security Platform to provide visibility and governance for enterprise AI deployments, bolstered by the acquisition of SurePath AI. The platform aims to mitigate risks associated with shadow AI by continuously monitoring and protecting AI models, agents, and their connecting APIs.

articles.summary: Attackers are exploiting Microsoft 365 collaboration tools and Outlook Groups to disguise phishing attempts as routine, trusted productivity workflows. This technique bypasses traditional security filters by embedding malicious actions within legitimate-looking notifications.

articles.summary: Attackers are distributing malicious VBScript files via WhatsApp Desktop and Web to install legitimate ManageEngine RMM software, enabling unauthorized remote access. The campaign is currently targeting users across multiple global regions.

articles.summary: Researchers developed EVOHUNT, a system that utilizes an optimized external playbook to enable AI agents to identify software vulnerabilities more effectively than OpenAI’s commercial Codex model at a significantly lower cost. articles.title: Five Eyes spooks warn AI means infosec incidents can become ‘major operational and financial crises’
articles.summary: The Five Eyes intelligence alliance has warned that AI-driven cyber threats are escalating, potentially transforming routine security incidents into severe operational and financial crises. Executives are urged to prioritize robust cybersecurity measures to mitigate these emerging risks.

articles.title: OpenAI Expands Daybreak With GPT-5.5-Cyber to Help Defenders Patch Security Flaws
articles.summary: OpenAI has launched an enhanced version of its GPT-5.5-Cyber model as part of the Daybreak initiative to assist cybersecurity defenders in identifying and patching complex software vulnerabilities. This tool is designed to perform deep code analysis to help secure large codebases.

articles.title: Sniff out stale AI override advice with this open source CLI
articles.summary: A new open-source CLI tool has been released to help developers identify and remediate stale AI override advice and insecure package dependencies. The tool focuses on mitigating vulnerabilities that are often difficult to detect within software supply chains.

articles.title: OpenAI: Yoo-hoo, look over here, we do that security stuff too!

articles.summary: Cloudflare has collaborated with major browser developers to implement Private Access Control Tokens, a mechanism designed to differentiate between human users and malicious bots. articles.summary: The FortiBleed campaign leveraged custom sniffer tools on compromised Fortinet FortiGate firewalls to harvest authentication credentials. This large-scale operation highlights a targeted effort to compromise network infrastructure to steal sensitive access data.

articles.title: Microsoft says Windows 11 26H2 is coming soon, details upgrade process
articles.summary: Microsoft has announced that Windows 11 26H2 is the upcoming feature update, which will be deployable for users on versions 24H2 and 25H2 via a lightweight enablement package.

articles.title: Microsoft fixes AutoGen Studio flaw that enabled code execution
articles.summary: Microsoft has patched a vulnerability chain called AutoJack in its AutoGen Studio interface that allowed attackers to execute arbitrary code on a host system through a malicious webpage. The flaw specifically targeted the prototyping tool for AI agents.

articles.title: Researchers Detail DifyTap Flaws in Dify That Could Expose AI Chats Across Tenants
articles.summary: Researchers identified four unauthenticated vulnerabilities in the Dify AI platform, collectively dubbed DifyTap, that allow unauthorized access to AI chat data across different tenants. These flaws pose a significant risk to data privacy for users of the open-source agentic workflow platform.

articles.title: Intel agencies: Frontier AI models will reshape cybersecurity faster than expected
articles.summary: Intelligence agencies from the Five Eyes alliance have issued a joint warning that frontier AI models are accelerating changes to the cybersecurity landscape more rapidly than previously anticipated. This advisory underscores growing global concerns regarding the dual-use nature of advanced artificial intelligence technologies.

articles.title: Texas Parks and Wildlife Data Breach Affects Over 3M License Customers
articles.summary: A third-party vendor breach has exposed the sensitive personal data, including driver's license and passport numbers, of approximately 3 million Texas Parks and Wildlife customers.

articles.title: 29-Year-Old Squid Proxy Bug 'Squidbleed' Can Leak Cleartext HTTP Requests
articles.summary: A 29-year-old heap over-read vulnerability dubbed 'Squidbleed' allows local attackers to intercept cleartext HTTP requests, including sensitive credentials, from other users on the same Squid proxy. The flaw, originating from a 1997 code change, remains present in default configurations.

articles.title: Canadian utility fesses up to data breach, but key details remain off-grid
articles.summary: London Hydro has confirmed a data breach potentially compromising customer names, addresses, and account details, though specific details regarding the incident remain undisclosed. The utility company is currently investigating the scope and nature of the intrusion.

articles.title: Threat Hunting Beyond Alerts: Finding the Activity Detection Misses
articles.summary: This article explores proactive threat hunting strategies designed to uncover malicious activity that automated security alerts and traditional detection systems often fail to identify.

articles.title: Suspected cyberattack triggers false emergency alerts across parts of Brazil
articles.summary: Unauthorized actors compromised Brazil's Civil Defense Alert system, resulting in the dissemination of false emergency notifications to the public. The incident highlights a security breach within a critical national infrastructure platform.

articles.title: A Glimpse into the “Search Your Target” Market for Stolen Credentials
articles.summary: The emergence of an underground market allows attackers to outsource the time-consuming process of searching large credential dumps for specific target data. This service lowers the barrier to entry for cybercriminals looking to acquire actionable intelligence on specific organizations.

articles.title: Anthropic’s Mythos AI broke into almost all NSA classified systems in hours
articles.summary: The Trump administration has ordered Anthropic to restrict access to its most powerful AI models, Mythos 5 and Fable 5, to U.S. citizens following allegations that the systems successfully breached NSA and Cyber Command networks. The move highlights the challenges of enforcing strict nationality-based access controls on rapidly evolving AI technologies.

articles.title: New OXLOADER Loader Uses Malicious Google Ads to Deliver CastleStealer
articles.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified a new malware loader called OXLOADER that uses malicious Google Ads to distribute the CastleStealer infostealer. The campaign is attributed to a likely Russian-speaking, financially motivated threat actor.

articles.title: Brazil probes emergency warning system after nationwide rogue alert
articles.summary: Brazilian authorities are investigating a security failure in the national emergency warning system that caused devices across the country to display the unauthorized word 'misanthropy'. The incident highlights a potential vulnerability in the country's public alert infrastructure.

articles.title: Scammers Use Fake GitHub Stars, VirusTotal Reviews to Spread Crypto Clipper
articles.summary: Cybercriminals are distributing a multi-platform crypto clipper malware by manipulating social proof metrics like fake GitHub stars and VirusTotal reviews to deceive Windows and Mac users. The malicious campaign embeds over 15,000 attacker-controlled wallets to facilitate the theft of cryptocurrency.

articles.title: Google Sets Sept. 30 Deadline for Android Developer Verification in Four Countries
articles.summary: Google will begin enforcing mandatory developer identity verification for Android apps in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand starting September 30, 2026. Apps from unverified developers will be blocked from installation on certified devices in these regions.

articles.title: Stop Your Legacy Infrastructure from Hijacking Your AI Agents
articles.summary: Security researchers are warning that attackers are bypassing modern AI security protocols by exploiting vulnerabilities within outdated legacy infrastructure. This emerging attack vector allows threat actors to hijack AI agents, highlighting a critical gap in current organizational security programs.

articles.title: Health board apologizes for phishing staff with with bogus vacation day
articles.summary: A Canadian health board issued an apology after conducting a phishing simulation that used a fake offer of extra vacation time to test employees. The incident drew criticism for exploiting the stress of medical workers during a sensitive period.

articles.title: Salesforce Disables Klue Integration After OAuth Token Theft Hits Customer Data
articles.summary: The Icarus extortion group exploited a legacy Klue credential to perform an OAuth token theft, resulting in unauthorized access to Salesforce data. In response, Salesforce has disabled the Klue integration to prevent further exfiltration.

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: Browser Bugs, EDR Killers, TV Botnet, OpenBSD Flaw, Android Trojan, and More
articles.summary: This weekly recap highlights a persistent landscape of cyber threats, including browser exploits, EDR evasion techniques, and mobile malware targeting users through deceptive downloads and weak security hygiene.

articles.title: FortiBleed: The Most Detailed Breakdown Yet of an Active Russian Credential-Harvesting Operation
articles.summary: The FortiBleed campaign has compromised over 430,000 FortiGate devices to harvest 110 million credentials, marking a major, ongoing Russian-linked cyber espionage operation. A comprehensive report from SOCRadar provides new technical insights into the scale and impact of this widespread credential-harvesting activity.

articles.title: Gizmodo readers hit with ClickFix malware prompts after account compromise
articles.summary: Gizmodo readers were targeted by a ClickFix malware campaign following a website account compromise that prompted Windows users to run malicious files. While Windows systems were at high risk, Mac users appeared to be unaffected by the specific payload.

articles.title: Canada’s Spy Agency Used First-of-Its-Kind Warrant to Clean Botnet-Infected Devices
articles.summary: The Canadian Security Intelligence Service successfully obtained a judicial warrant to remotely neutralize foreign-run botnets by modifying infected local servers, routers, and IoT devices. This marks the first time the agency has utilized threat reduction powers to directly intervene in compromised civilian infrastructure.

articles.title: 4,300+ Outdated Routers Hijacked in Stealthy Spy Infrastructure by AryStinger malware
articles.summary: The AryStinger malware has compromised over 4,300 outdated routers by exploiting long-standing vulnerabilities to establish a stealthy infrastructure for reconnaissance and cyber-espionage. Security researchers identified the campaign after tracking a binary spreading through flaws dating back to 2013 and 2016.

articles.title: 23 ClawHub plugins squatting official scopes expose AI registry security gaps
articles.summary: Twenty-three malicious plugins were discovered using official 'ClawHub' and 'OpenClaw' scopes to execute unauthorized code, highlighting significant security vulnerabilities in AI agent plugin registries. The incident underscores a lack of scope reservation controls that allows attackers to impersonate official publishers.

articles.title: usbliter8 Brings Unpatchable BootROM Exploit to Apple A12 and A13 Devices
articles.summary: Security researchers have released usbliter8, an unpatchable BootROM exploit targeting Apple's A12 and A13 chips that enables arbitrary code execution within the SecureROM. This vulnerability extends critical security risks similar to the checkm8 exploit to a wider range of newer iPhone devices.

articles.title: AryStinger Malware Infects 4,300 Legacy Routers to Build Reconnaissance Proxy Network
articles.summary: A new malware family called AryStinger has compromised over 4,300 legacy routers to establish a distributed reconnaissance and proxy network for pre-attack staging. Unlike typical router botnets, this strain focuses on stealthy network intelligence rather than DDoS operations.

articles.title: INTERPOL Warns Phishing, Ransomware, and AI Scams Are Rising Across Asia-Pacific
articles.summary: INTERPOL's latest report identifies a significant surge in cybercrime across the Asia-Pacific region, driven by rapid digital transformation and the exploitation of emerging technologies like AI. Phishing, ransomware, and AI-enabled scams are highlighted as the primary threats facing the area.

articles.title: Who pays when you gate cyber-capable AI models?
articles.summary: Jaya Baloo discusses the debate over restricting access to cyber-capable AI models, arguing that policymakers fail to consider how such gates may disadvantage security teams and widen the capability gap between attackers and defenders.

articles.title: Agent Beacon: Open-source telemetry layer for AI agents
articles.summary: Agent Beacon is a new open-source telemetry tool designed to monitor and normalize activity logs for AI coding agents running across local, CI, and cloud environments. It aims to improve visibility into the actions, commands, and tool calls executed by AI development agents.

articles.title: Encrypted DNS still tells an eavesdropper where to look
articles.summary: While encrypted DNS protocols protect the contents of queries, researchers highlight that plaintext packet headers still expose user browsing habits to network eavesdroppers. The study specifically evaluates this information leakage within Internet of Things (IoT) environments.

articles.title: Product showcase: Avira Security for iOS blends security, privacy, and device optimization
articles.summary: Avira has released an updated security application for iOS that integrates privacy, security, and device optimization tools into a single platform. The app is designed to improve user experience through a streamlined onboarding process and customizable privacy settings.

articles.title: Hundreds of AI-powered iOS apps found exposing credentials
articles.summary: Researchers at Wake Forest University discovered that 282 out of 444 analyzed iOS apps with AI features leaked exploitable LLM API credentials through network traffic. This vulnerability exposes backend access mechanisms across numerous application categories.

articles.title: The systemd 261 release brings a software TPM, new OS installer
articles.summary: The release of systemd 261 introduces new features including a software TPM, an OS installer, and a cloud metadata subsystem (systemd-imdsd). These updates aim to enhance cloud instance management and system initialization capabilities for Linux distributions.

articles.title: SECURITY AFFAIRS MALWARE NEWSLETTER ROUND 102
articles.summary: The Security Affairs Malware Newsletter summarizes recent cyber threats, including a major supply chain attack on OptinMonster affecting 1.2 million sites and ongoing espionage campaigns by China-nexus actors targeting research sectors.

articles.title: Security Affairs newsletter Round 582 by Pierluigi Paganini – INTERNATIONAL EDITION
articles.summary: The 582nd edition of the Security Affairs newsletter features analysis on the GentleKiller EDR-killer, a Fortinet credential-spraying campaign, and active CISA warnings. It serves as a weekly digest of significant cybersecurity developments and threat intelligence.

articles.title: AryStinger botnet infected thousands of D-Link routers worldwide
articles.summary: The newly discovered AryStinger botnet has compromised over 4,000 outdated D-Link routers, repurposing them as proxies for malicious traffic. These devices are being exploited due to their lack of current security patches.

articles.title: Week in review: 74k Fortinet firewall credentials stolen, Splunk Enterprise RCE under active attack
articles.summary: Recent cybersecurity news highlights the theft of 74,000 Fortinet firewall credentials, active exploitation of a Splunk Enterprise RCE vulnerability, and the discovery of a hardware-level backdoor attack named HAMLOCK.

articles.title: Inside GentleKiller: The EDR-Killer Powering The Gentlemen
articles.summary: The cybercriminal group 'The Gentlemen' is utilizing a sophisticated EDR-killing tool called 'GentleKiller' that leverages BYOVD exploits to disable security software before deploying ransomware. This technical infrastructure was detailed in an ESET investigation following a significant internal data leak.

articles.title: Inside GentleKiller: The EDR-Killer Powering The Gentlemen
articles.summary: The cybercrime group known as The Gentlemen is utilizing a sophisticated EDR-killer tool called GentleKiller to neutralize security software via BYOVD exploits prior to launching ransomware attacks. ESET researchers recently detailed the group's infrastructure, which was further confirmed by internal data leaks.

articles.title: New Prinz Eugen ransomware prioritizes recent files for encryption
articles.summary: The Prinz Eugen ransomware is a newly identified operation that targets recently modified files for encryption while notably omitting ransom notes. This stealthy behavior suggests a focus on rapid data impact during active intrusions.

articles.title: Why Amazon hates 'human-in-the-loop' AI governance
articles.summary: Amazon VP Eric Brandwine argues that human-in-the-loop AI governance is inefficient because human decision-making is prone to error and scalability issues. The perspective suggests a shift toward more automated oversight mechanisms within corporate AI policy.

articles.title: Microsoft links Mastra AI supply chain attack to North Korean hackers
articles.summary: Microsoft has attributed a supply chain attack involving over 140 compromised npm packages to the North Korean state-sponsored threat group Sapphire Sleet. The incident highlights the ongoing risk of malicious software packages being used for unauthorized system access.

articles.title: MDR Provider Comparison: Time to Discover and Respond to Threats
articles.summary: This guide provides a comprehensive comparison of Managed Detection and Response (MDR) providers, focusing on key performance metrics like response speed and threat intelligence capabilities to assist organizations in vendor selection.

articles.title: Hackers Exploit Gravity SMTP WordPress Plugin Bug to Expose API Keys
articles.summary: Hackers are actively exploiting a medium-severity vulnerability in the Gravity SMTP WordPress plugin to extract sensitive information, including API keys and OAuth tokens. Users are advised to update their installations to mitigate the risk of data exposure.

articles.title: FortiBleed Exposes Global Credential-Spraying Operation
articles.summary: A massive industrial-scale credential-spraying campaign targeted global Fortinet VPN devices, resulting in widespread organizational compromises. The attack was discovered by security researcher Volodymyr Diachenko due to the threat actors' operational negligence.

articles.title: CISA Warns of Active Exploitation Following FortiBleed Leak
articles.summary: CISA has issued an emergency alert following the leak of credentials for approximately 74,000 Fortinet devices, which are currently being actively exploited by threat actors. This security incident, dubbed 'FortiBleed,' affects various firewalls and VPN gateways worldwide.

articles.title: Threat Brief: Mitigating Large-Scale Credential Attacks
articles.summary: Unit 42 provides strategic guidance for defending against large-scale credential stuffing attacks, specifically addressing recent campaigns that target security vendor infrastructure.

articles.title: Klue OAuth breach victim list grows as Icarus hackers claim attack
articles.summary: Market intelligence platform Klue confirmed a security incident involving the theft of OAuth tokens connected to customer Salesforce environments, with the Icarus extortion group claiming responsibility. The breach has led to an expanding list of affected organizations.

articles.title: Hackers exploit info disclosure bug in Gravity SMTP WordPress plugin
articles.summary: Hackers are actively exploiting an unauthenticated information disclosure vulnerability within the Gravity SMTP WordPress plugin, which is installed on over 100,000 websites.

articles.title: Unpatchable 'usbliter8' Exploit Breaks Apple A12 and A13 SecureROM Boot Chain
articles.summary: Security researchers have discovered an unpatchable exploit called 'usbliter8' affecting the SecureROM of Apple's A12 and A13 chips, allowing for arbitrary code execution. Because the vulnerability is tied to the hardware, it cannot be mitigated via software updates.

articles.title: The Gentlemen RaaS Uses GentleKiller EDR Framework Targeting 400 Security Processes
articles.summary: The Gentlemen ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) group is distributing a sophisticated framework called GentleKiller, which enables affiliates to terminate over 400 security processes to bypass endpoint detection. This development highlights the growing trend of threat actors utilizing specialized EDR-killing tools to facilitate ransomware deployment.

articles.title: Meteor 3.0 Migration Helped Rocket.Chat Move Off End-of-Life Node.js Runtime
articles.summary: Rocket.Chat migrated to Meteor 3.0 to upgrade its underlying Node.js runtime from version 14 to 20. This update effectively resolves technical debt associated with the removal of Fibers and mitigates supply-chain security risks for federal users.

articles.title: Texas govt data breach exposes over 3 million driver’s licenses
articles.summary: The Texas Parks and Wildlife Department suffered a data breach involving a third-party vendor, resulting in the exposure of personal information for over three million driver's license holders. The incident highlights the risks associated with supply chain security for government entities.

articles.title: Researchers drop checkm8-style BootROM exploit for A12 and A13 iPhones
articles.summary: Security researchers have released a permanent, unpatchable BootROM exploit affecting A12 and A13 chipsets in certain iPhone models. Because the flaw exists at the hardware level, it cannot be fixed via software updates.

articles.title: AutoJack Attack Lets One Web Page Hijack AI Agent for Host Code Execution
articles.summary: Microsoft researchers discovered AutoJack, a vulnerability that allows malicious web pages to exploit AI browsing agents to execute arbitrary code on a host machine. The attack bypasses authentication and requires no user interaction after the initial page load.

articles.title: Operation Endgame Disrupts SocGholish Servers, Cleans 14,971 WordPress Sites
articles.summary: International law enforcement agencies collaborated in Operation Endgame to dismantle SocGholish malicious infrastructure, resulting in the cleanup of nearly 15,000 compromised WordPress websites.

articles.title: Gcore Helps Ucom Safeguard Public Live Broadcast Infrastructure During Armenia’s Parliamentary Elections
articles.summary: Gcore provided infrastructure protection services to Ucom to secure public live broadcasting during Armenia's parliamentary elections. The collaboration focused on safeguarding critical communications against potential cyber disruptions during a sensitive political event.

articles.title: CISA Warns Fortinet Customers as FortiBleed Hits 86,644 FortiGate Devices
articles.summary: CISA has issued an urgent warning to Fortinet customers regarding the 'FortiBleed' campaign, which has compromised over 86,000 internet-accessible FortiGate devices. The campaign is attributed to Russian-speaking threat actors, prompting authorities to advise immediate patching and security measures.

articles.title: Nintendo America Employee Data Exposed After Shadowbyt3$ Targets TinyPulse
articles.summary: The hacker group Shadowbyt3 breached the employee engagement platform TinyPulse, resulting in the exposure of sensitive HR and financial records belonging to Nintendo of America staff. The compromised data includes tax forms, banking details, and internal survey responses.

articles.title: 14,971 WordPress Sites Cleaned in Global SocGholish Takedown
articles.summary: Law enforcement agencies from four countries conducted Operation EndGame, successfully dismantling the SocGholish malware infrastructure and cleaning nearly 15,000 infected WordPress sites.

articles.title: eFAQ Publishes Investigation Into Alleged Scam Activity and Coordinated Reputation Attacks
articles.summary: eFAQ has released an investigative report detailing allegations of scam operations and orchestrated campaigns designed to damage reputations. The report highlights the impact of coordinated disinformation efforts on digital trust.

articles.title: Every AI Agent Is an Identity. Most Organizations Don't Treat Them That Way
articles.summary: AI agents now possess significant operational capabilities within corporate environments, yet they often lack the robust identity management and governance protocols required to secure them. This creates a critical security gap as these autonomous systems become high-value targets for attackers.

articles.title: Everything's bigger and better in Texas – even data breaches
articles.summary: A data breach involving Texas hunting and fishing licenses has exposed the personal information of approximately 3 million residents. The incident highlights a significant security failure affecting a large portion of the state's population.

articles.title: Klue breach lead to Salesforce data theft, Huntress affected
articles.summary: A security breach at market intelligence platform Klue led to the compromise of integration credentials, resulting in unauthorized access and data theft from connected services like Salesforce for companies including Huntress. The incident highlights the risks of a supply chain attack cascading through third-party integrations.

articles.title: Police raid malware network tied to Russia's Evil Corp hacker group
articles.summary: An international law enforcement operation has successfully targeted the SocGholish botnet, a malware distribution network associated with the Russian-based cybercrime organization Evil Corp.

articles.title: Webinar: How attackers bypass MFA and how defenders can respond
articles.summary: This webinar examines how modern phishing techniques like Device Code attacks bypass MFA and discusses using behavioral AI to detect and automate responses to compromised accounts.

articles.title: Cybercriminals abused GitHub, YouTube and VirusTotal to push crypto-stealing malware
articles.summary: Cybercriminals are using a multi-platform campaign on GitHub, YouTube, and VirusTotal to distribute crypto-stealing malware disguised as legitimate trading and gambling tools. By manipulating platform metrics and feedback, the attackers successfully built a false sense of trust to deceive users.
